name: Physics
topics: Scalars and vectors, resolution of forces
Motion: speed, velocity, acceleration and equations of motion
Pressure in solids, liquids and gases; Archimedes' principle and flotation
Quantity of heat: specific heat capacity and latent heat
Light: reflection at plane and curved mirrors
Refraction, total internal reflection and lenses
Current electricity: Ohm's law, resistors in series and parallel, e.m.f.
Electrical energy and power, cost of electricity
Atomic and nuclear physics: radioactivity and half-life

questions.q: Which of the following physical quantities is a derived quantity?
questions.e: Magnetic flux is a derived quantity because it is defined in terms of magnetic field strength and area, whereas electric current, luminous intensity, and amount of substance are fundamental SI quantities.
questions.p: Na magnetic flux be derived quantity because dem dey calculate am from other basic units, while the other three na fundamental quantities for SI system.

questions.q: The dimensions of pressure in terms of mass [M], length [L], and time [T] are:
questions.e: Pressure is defined as force per unit area. Force has dimensions [M][L][T]⁻² and area has dimensions [L]², giving pressure the dimensional formula [M][L]⁻¹[T]⁻².
questions.p: Pressure na force divided by area. When you divide force dimension [M][L][T]⁻² by area dimension [L]², you go get [M][L]⁻¹[T]⁻².

questions.q: A student measures the length of a physics laboratory table using a metre rule and records 1.45 m. If the actual length of the table is 1.40 m, what is the percentage error of the measurement?
questions.e: Percentage error is calculated as (Measured value - Actual value) / Actual value × 100%. Here, (1.45 - 1.40) / 1.40 × 100% = 0.05 / 1.40 × 100% = 3.57%.
questions.p: Percentage error na error divided by true value multiply by 100. So na (1.45 - 1.40) over 1.40 times 100, wey give us 3.57 percent.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of the physical quantity whose dimension is [M][L]²[T]⁻²?
questions.e: Work or energy is defined as force multiplied by displacement, which has the dimension [M][L][T]⁻² × [L] = [M][L]²[T]⁻², and its SI unit is the Joule.
questions.p: Work or energy get dimension [M][L]⁻²[T]⁻² and na Joule be the SI unit for am.

questions.q: The period T of a simple pendulum of length l is given by T = 2pi × √(l / g), where g is the acceleration due to gravity. If the measured length has a maximum fractional error of 2 percent and the period has a fractional error of 1 percent, what is the maximum percentage error in the calculated value of g?
questions.e: From g = 4pi² × l / T², the fractional error is delta(g)/g = delta(l)/l + 2(delta(T)/T). Substituting the values gives 2% + 2(1%) = 4%.
questions.p: From the formula for g, percentage error for g na percentage error of length plus two times percentage error of period. Dat na 2 plus 2 times 1, wey give us 4 percent.

questions.q: A micrometer screw gauge with a zero error of +0.03 mm is used to measure the diameter of a thin copper wire. If the main scale reading is 1.50 mm and the circular scale reading is 28 divisions (where 1 division = 0.01 mm), what is the true diameter of the wire?
questions.e: Observed reading = 1.50 mm + (28 × 0.01 mm) = 1.78 mm. True reading = Observed reading - Zero error = 1.78 mm - 0.03 mm = 1.75 mm.
questions.p: First find the reading wey you see by adding main scale and circular scale to get 1.78 mm. Then minus the positive zero error of 0.03 mm to get the true reading of 1.75 mm.

questions.q: Which of the following instruments is most suitable and precise for measuring the internal diameter of a small test tube?
questions.e: Vernier callipers have internal jaws specifically designed to measure internal diameters accurately up to 0.01 cm or 0.1 mm, making them more precise than a metre rule.
questions.p: Na Vernier callipers dem dey use measure internal diameter well well because e get small jaws wey fit enter inside pipe or test tube.

questions.q: The velocity v of a wave on a string depends on the tension T, the length l, and the mass m of the string. If v = k × Tˣ × lʸ × mᶻ where k is a dimensionless constant, what are the values of x, y, and z?
questions.e: Using dimensional analysis, [LT⁻¹] = ([MLT⁻²])ˣ [L]ʸ [M]ᶻ. Equating powers of M: x + z = 0; L: x + y = 1; T: -2x = -1. Solving gives x = 1/2, z = -1/2, and y = 1/2.
questions.p: Make you use dimension balance both sides. When you match powers for Mass, Length, and Time, you go get x = 1/2, y = 1/2, and z = -1/2.

questions.q: An office block in Abuja has a floor area of 250 m². Express this area in cm² in standard scientific notation.
questions.e: Since 1 m = 100 cm, 1 m² = (100 cm)² = 10,000 cm² = 10⁴ cm². Therefore, 250 m² = 250 × 10⁴ cm² = 2.50 × 10⁶ cm².
questions.p: Because 1 metre na 100 cm, 1 square metre na 10,000 square cm. Multiply 250 by 10,000 to get 2,500,000, wey be 2.50 times 10 power 6.

questions.q: Which of the following physical quantities is completely specified by magnitude alone?
questions.e: Electric potential is a scalar quantity because it only has magnitude and no specific direction in space. The other three quantities possess both magnitude and direction, making them vectors.
questions.p: Electric potential na scalar quantity because e get only magnitude and no direction. The remaining three na vectors because dem get both magnitude and direction.

questions.q: Two forces of magnitudes 6 N and 8 N act at a point at right angles to each other. What is the magnitude of their resultant force?
questions.e: Since the forces are at right angles, the resultant R is given by √(6² + 8²). This evaluates to √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 N.
questions.p: Because the two forces dey perpendicular to each other, we go use Pythagoras theorem. R = √(6² + 8²) wey give us 10 N.

questions.q: A force vector F = (3i + 4j) N acts on a body. What is the angle theta the force makes with the positive x-axis?
questions.e: The angle theta is given by arctan(F_y / F_x) = arctan(4 / 3). This evaluates to approximately 53.13 degrees, which rounds to 53°.
questions.p: To find the angle, we use tan(theta) = y-component / x-component, na 4 / 3. When you find inverse tan of 1.333, you go get about 53 degrees.

questions.q: A body of weight 50 N is pulled along a smooth horizontal floor by a string inclined at an angle of 60° to the horizontal. If the tension in the string is 40 N, what is the horizontal component of the pulling force?
questions.e: The horizontal component of a force F at angle theta is F × cos(theta). Here, it is 40cos(60°) = 40 × 0.5 = 20 N.
questions.p: To find the horizontal component, na F cos(theta). So na 40 multiply by cos(60°), and cos(60) na 0.5. 40 times 0.5 go give us 20 N.

questions.q: A block rests on an inclined plane making an angle of 30° with the horizontal. The component of the weight of the block parallel to the inclined plane, given a weight W, is:
questions.e: When resolving weight on an inclined plane, the component parallel to the slope is always W × sin(theta), where theta is the angle of inclination.
questions.p: Wetin dey pull the block down the slope na the component parallel to the plane, and na W sin(theta). For this case, theta na 30°.

questions.q: Three coplanar forces of 3 N, 4 N, and 5 N act on an object such that their vector sum is zero. What is the angle between the 3 N and 4 N forces?
questions.e: Since 3² + 4² = 5², the 3 N and 4 N forces form a right-angled triangle with the 5 N force acting as the equilibrant. Therefore, the angle between the 3 N and 4 N forces must be 90°.
questions.p: If you check 3, 4 and 5, dem fit form right-angled triangle because 3² + 4² = 5². That mean say the 3 N and 4 N forces dey perpendicular to each other, so the angle na 90 degrees.

questions.q: A boat is steered across a flowing river with a velocity of 6 m/s due north. The river flows due east with a velocity of 8 m/s. What is the magnitude of the resultant velocity of the boat?
questions.e: The boat's velocity and the river's velocity are perpendicular. The resultant velocity is √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 m/s.
questions.p: The boat velocity and river current dey perpendicular, so we use Pythagoras theorem. V_resultant = √(6² + 8²) = 10 m/s.

questions.q: A commercial bus in Onitsha accelerates uniformly from rest at 3 m/s² for 4 seconds. Calculate the final velocity of the bus.
questions.e: Use the first equation of motion, v = u + at. Given initial velocity u = 0, acceleration a = 3 m/s², and time t = 4 s, the final velocity v = 0 + (3 × 4) = 12 m/s.
questions.p: Make you use the first formula v = u + at. Since motor start from rest (u = 0), you multiply acceleration (3) by time (4) to get 12 m/s.

questions.q: Which of the following physical quantities is a vector?
questions.e: Average velocity has both magnitude and a specific direction, making it a vector quantity. Speed, distance, and time only have magnitude and are scalars.
questions.p: Na only average velocity get both magnitude and direction, na why im be vector quantity. The remaining three na scalars because dem get magnitude alone.

questions.q: A tricycle (Keke Napep) moving along a straight Lagos road changes its velocity from 10 m/s to 22 m/s in 6 seconds. What is its average acceleration?
questions.e: Acceleration a = (v - u) / t. Substituting the values, a = (22 - 10) / 6 = 12 / 6 = 2 m/s².
questions.p: To find acceleration, minus initial velocity from final velocity and divide by time. So na (22 minus 10) divide by 6, wey give 12 over 6 = 2 m/s².

questions.q: An object starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 2 m/s². How far does it travel in the 3rd second of its motion?
questions.e: The distance traveled in the nth second is given by S_nth = u + a/2(2n - 1). With u = 0, a = 2, and n = 3, S_3rd = 0 + (2/2) × (2(3) - 1) = 1(6 - 1) = 5 m.
questions.p: For distance wey object cover for just one particular second n, use formula S = u + (a/2)(2n - 1). Put u = 0, a = 2, and n = 3, you go get 5 meters.

questions.q: A student drops a stone from the top of a storey building in Ibadan. If it hits the ground after 3 seconds, calculate the height of the building. (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.e: Use the second equation of motion for free fall, h = ut + (1/2)gt². Since u = 0, h = 0.5 × 10 × 3² = 5 × 9 = 45 m.
questions.p: Since stone fall freely from rest, u = 0. Use h = ut + 0.5gt², multiply half of gravity (5) by square of time (3 squared = 9), you get 45 meters.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about a body moving with uniform velocity is correct?
o: Its acceleration is constant and non-zero.
Its displacement changes at a constant rate.
questions.e: Uniform velocity means equal displacements occur in equal time intervals, so displacement changes at a constant rate while acceleration is zero.
questions.p: If body dey move with uniform velocity, e dey cover equal distance for equal time for same direction. Dat mean im displacement dey change at constant rate and acceleration na zero.

questions.q: A car travelling at 20 m/s applies its brakes and comes to a halt over a distance of 50 m. Assuming uniform deceleration, what is the magnitude of the deceleration?
questions.e: Use v² = u² + 2as. Here v = 0, u = 20, and s = 50. So 0 = 20² + 2a × 50, which gives 400 + 100a = 0, leading to a = -400 / 100 = -4 m/s². The magnitude is 4 m/s².
questions.p: Make you apply v squared = u squared + 2as. Put 0 for final velocity, 20 for initial, and 50 for distance. You go solve find a, wey go give minus 4 m/s², meaning magnitude na 4.

questions.q: The slope of a displacement-time graph at any given point represents which of the following quantities?
questions.e: By definition, the derivative of displacement with respect to time is velocity. Therefore, the slope of a displacement-time graph at any point gives the instantaneous velocity.
questions.p: Na definition of displacement-time graph be say the gradient or slope for any point na the instantaneous velocity of the object.

questions.q: A particle moves along a straight line such that its displacement s in meters is given by s = t³ - 3t² + 4. Find the acceleration of the particle at t = 2 seconds.
questions.e: Velocity v = ds/dt = 3t² - 6t. Acceleration a = dv/dt = 6t - 6. Substituting t = 2 seconds, a = 6(2) - 6 = 12 - 6 = 6 m/s².
questions.p: You go differentiate displacement equation once to get velocity (v = 3t² - 6t), then differentiate am again to get acceleration (a = 6t - 6). Put t = 2 inside, you go get 6 m/s².

questions.q: A student in Enugu kicks a football from the ground with an initial velocity of 20 m/s at an angle of 30° to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is the maximum height reached by the football?
questions.e: The maximum height of a projectile is given by H = (u² × sin²(theta)) / (2g). Substituting u = 20, theta = 30°, and g = 10 gives H = (400(0.5)²) / 20 = 100 / 20 = 5.0 m.
questions.p: To find maximum height, you use the formula H = (u² × sin²(theta)) / (2g). When you put 20 for u and 30° for theta, you go get 5.0 meters.

questions.q: Which of the following physical quantities remains constant throughout the flight of an idealized projectile launched near the Earth's surface, assuming air resistance is completely negligible?
questions.e: Since air resistance is ignored, there is no horizontal force acting on the projectile. Therefore, the horizontal component of acceleration is zero, making the horizontal velocity remain constant throughout the flight.
questions.p: As air resistance no dey, nothing dey push or pull the object for sideways. Na why the speed wey dey go side (horizontal velocity) dey remain constant all through.

questions.q: A stone is tied to a string of length 0.5 m and whirled in a vertical circle with a uniform speed of 4 m/s. What is the centripetal acceleration of the stone?
questions.e: Centripetal acceleration is given by a = v² / r. Substituting v = 4 m/s and r = 0.5 m, we get a = 4² / 0.5 = 16 / 0.5 = 32 m/s².
questions.p: To calculate centripetal acceleration, use a = v² over r. When you square 4 and divide by 0.5, your answer go be 32 m/s².

questions.q: An object is projected horizontally from the top of a tower with a speed of 15 m/s and hits the ground 3 seconds later. What is the height of the tower? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.e: The vertical height of a horizontally launched projectile is determined entirely by free fall: h = (1/2) × g × t². With g = 10 and t = 3, h = 0.5 × 10 × 3² = 45 m.
questions.p: Because na drop e drop for vertical side, you use h = 1/2 gt². Put 10 for g and 3 for time, you go get 45 meters.

questions.q: At what angle of projection does a projectile achieve its maximum horizontal range on level ground, assuming initial speed is constant?
questions.e: The range of a projectile is R = (u² × sin(2theta)) / g. The sine function reaches its maximum value of 1 when the angle is 90°, meaning 2theta = 90°, so theta = 45°.
questions.p: To throw something go far reach maximum range, the angle must be 45 degrees because sin(90) na 1.

questions.q: A car of mass 1000 kg moves around a circular track of radius 20 m with a constant speed. If the maximum frictional force the tires can provide is 5000 N before skidding, what is the maximum safe speed of the car?
questions.e: The frictional force supplies the necessary centripetal force: F = (m × v²) / r. Rearranging gives v = √((F × r) / m) = √((5000 × 20) / 1000) = √100 = 10 m/s.
questions.p: Na friction dey provide the centripetal force. Make you use v = square root of (F times r over m), you go get 10 meters per second.

questions.q: A particle is projected with a speed of 50 m/s at an angle of 30° to the horizontal. What is the total time of flight? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.e: The total time of flight for a projectile is T = (2u × sin(theta)) / g. Substituting u = 50, theta = 30°, and g = 10 gives T = (2 × 50 × 0.5) / 10 = 50 / 10 = 5.0 s.
questions.p: Time of flight formula na T = (2 u sin theta) / g. When you calculate am, 2 times 50 times 0.5 divide by 10 give you 5 seconds.

questions.q: Two projectiles, A and B, are launched from the same point on level ground with the same initial speed. Projectile A is launched at 25° and projectile B is launched at 65° to the horizontal. Which of the following statements is true about their horizontal ranges?
o: Range of A is equal to range of B
Range of A is greater than range of B
Range of A is twice the range of B
Range of A is less than range of B
questions.e: Complementary angles of projection (angles that sum to 90°) yield the exact same horizontal range. Since 25° + 65° = 90°, their ranges are equal.
questions.p: Any two angles wey add up give 90 degrees go get the same range. Because 25 plus 65 na 90, their ranges must be equal.

questions.q: A body moves in a circular path of radius 2 m with a constant frequency of 0.5 revolutions per second. What is the magnitude of its linear speed?
questions.e: Linear speed v is related to radius r and frequency f by the formula v = 2pi × r × f. Given r = 2 m and f = 0.5 Hz, we find v = 2pi × 2 × 0.5 = 2.0 π m/s.
questions.p: Linear speed formula for circular motion na v = 2 π r f. Just multiply 2 by π by radius 2 by frequency 0.5, you go get 2.0 π m/s.

questions.q: Which of the following physical quantities is defined as the rate of change of momentum?
questions.e: According to Newton's second law of motion, the net force acting on a body is directly proportional to the rate of change of its momentum.
questions.p: Na according to Newton second law of motion wey talk say force na di rate of change of momentum.

questions.q: A body of mass 4 kg moving with a velocity of 5 m/s collides head-on with a stationary body of mass 6 kg. If they stick together after the collision, calculate their common velocity.
questions.e: Using the principle of conservation of linear momentum: (4 × 5) + (6 × 0) = (4 + 6) × v. Therefore, 20 = 10v, giving v = 2.0 m/s.
questions.p: We go use conservation of momentum: total momentum before equal total momentum after. E go be (4 times 5) plus zero equal to (4 plus 6) times v, so v na 2.0 m/s.

questions.q: A constant force of 15 N is applied to a stationary block of mass 3 kg on a smooth horizontal surface for 2 seconds. What is the final momentum of the block?
questions.e: Impulse is equal to change in momentum. Impulse = Force × time = 15 N × 2 s = 30 kg m/s. Since initial momentum is zero, final momentum is 30 kg m/s.
questions.p: Impulse na change in momentum, and e equal to Force times time. So na 15 times 2, wey give us 30 kg m/s.

questions.q: Why does a goalkeeper pull his hands backward when catching a fast-moving football?
o: To prevent the ball from spinning
To increase the impact force on his hands
To decrease the momentum of the ball to zero instantly
To increase the time of impact, thereby reducing the force
questions.e: Pulling the hands back increases the time interval during which the momentum of the ball is reduced. Since force is change in momentum divided by time, a larger time results in a smaller impact force.
questions.p: When goalkeeper draw im hand back, e dey increase di time wey di ball take stop. Di more di time, di small di force wey go pain im hand.

questions.q: An object of mass 2 kg falls freely from rest under gravity and hits the ground with a velocity of 20 m/s. If it rebounds with a velocity of 10 m/s, calculate the magnitude of the impulse received by the object from the ground.
questions.e: Impulse = final momentum - initial momentum = m(v - u). Taking upward direction as positive, Impulse = 2(10 - (-20)) = 2 × 30 = 60 N s.
questions.p: Impulse na final momentum minus initial momentum. Make we remember say direction matter, so na mass times (final velocity minus minus initial velocity), wey be 2 times (10 minus minus 20) = 60 N s.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes Newton's first law of motion?
o: The total momentum of a closed system is always conserved.
An object continues in its state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled by an external force.
Acceleration is directly proportional to the applied force.
To every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
questions.e: Newton's first law is also known as the law of inertia, stating that bodies maintain their state of motion unless acted upon by an external net force.
questions.p: Newton first law talk about inertia, say body go remain for where e dey or dey move straight until external force come pursue am.

questions.q: A bullet of mass 50 g is fired horizontally with a velocity of 400 m/s into a stationary wooden block of mass 1.95 kg resting on a smooth surface. If the bullet embeds itself in the block, find the common velocity of the system.
questions.e: Convert mass of bullet to kg: 50 g = 0.05 kg. Using conservation of momentum: (0.05 × 400) + (1.95 × 0) = (0.05 + 1.95) × v. Thus, 20 = 2.0v, giving v = 10.0 m/s.
questions.p: First convert 50g to kg to get 0.05 kg. Apply conservation of momentum: (0.05 times 400) equal to (0.05 plus 1.95) times v. You get 20 equal to 2v, so v na 10.0 m/s.

questions.q: A cart of mass 5 kg is accelerated uniformly from rest at 3 m/s² along a flat floor. What is the magnitude of the net force acting on the cart?
questions.e: Using Newton's second law, Force = mass × acceleration. F = 5 kg × 3 m/s² = 15.0 N.
questions.p: Just use direct formula from Newton second law: Force = mass times acceleration. Na 5 times 3, wey give us 15.0 N.

questions.q: A student in Onitsha carries a bag of rice of mass 20 kg up a flight of stairs of height 5 m in 10 seconds. Taking acceleration due to gravity g as 10 m/s², what is the power developed by the student?
questions.e: Power is the rate of doing work, calculated as (mass x gravity x height) divided by time taken. Substituting the values gives (20 x 10 x 5) / 10, which equals 100 Watts.
questions.p: Power na work divided by time, wey be (mass times gravity times height) over time. When you put the numbers inside, (20 times 10 times 5) divide by 10 go give you 100 Watts.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes between conservative and non-conservative forces?
o: Gravitational force is an example of a non-conservative force, while friction is a conservative force.
The work done by a conservative force along a closed path is zero, unlike a non-conservative force.
Conservative forces dissipate mechanical energy into heat, while non-conservative forces do not.
Non-conservative forces depend only on the initial and final positions of an object.
questions.e: A conservative force is one where the work done in moving an object between two points is independent of the path taken, meaning the work done along a closed loop is zero. Friction and air resistance are typical non-conservative forces that do not share this property.
questions.p: Conservative force na the one wey work wey e do no dey depend on road wey person follow, so if you carry something go back where e start, total work na zero. Friction and air resistance na non-conservative because energy dey lost for road.

questions.q: An engine pumps water from a borehole in Ibadan at a rate of 60 kg per minute to a height of 10 m. If g = 10 m/s², what is the useful output power of the engine?
questions.e: First, find the mass per second, which is 60 kg / 60 s = 1 kg/s. Power is (mass/time) x g x h, which evaluates to 1 x 10 x 10 = 100 Watts.
questions.p: First find mass per second, wey be 60 kg divide by 60 seconds to get 1 kg per second. Then multiply am by gravity (10) and height (10) to get 100 Watts.

questions.q: A brick of mass 2 kg is dropped from a height of 15 m above the ground. Using g = 10 m/s², what is its kinetic energy just before it hits the floor, assuming air resistance is negligible?
questions.e: By the principle of conservation of mechanical energy, the initial potential energy equals the final kinetic energy. Potential energy is mgh = 2 x 10 x 15 = 300 Joules.
questions.p: Because energy no dey lost, all the potential energy wey the brick get for top go turn to kinetic energy when e wan touch ground. Just multiply mass (2), gravity (10) and height (15) to get 300 Joules.

questions.q: A block is pulled across a rough horizontal floor by a constant force of 50 N acting at an angle of 60 degrees to the horizontal. How much work is done by the force in moving the block a distance of 8 m? (Given cos(60°) = 0.5)
questions.e: Work done is given by W = F x d x cos(theta). Substituting the values, W = 50 x 8 x cos(60°) = 50 x 8 x 0.5 = 200 Joules.
questions.p: Work done na Force times distance times cos(theta). Put the numbers inside: 50 times 8 times 0.5, e go give you 200 Joules.

questions.q: A light spring of natural length 0.2 m is stretched by a force of 40 N to a length of 0.3 m. How much elastic potential energy is stored in the stretched spring?
questions.e: The extension x = 0.3 - 0.2 = 0.1 m. The spring constant k = F / x = 40 / 0.1 = 400 N/m. The energy stored is 0.5 x k x x² = 0.5 x 400 x (0.1)² = 2.0 Joules.
questions.p: First find extension, wey be 0.3 minus 0.2 to get 0.1 m. Find k as 40 over 0.1 to get 400 N/m, then use energy formula 0.5 times k times x square to get 2.0 Joules.

questions.q: Which of the following physical quantities has the same SI unit as work?
questions.e: Work is defined as force multiplied by displacement, measured in Joules (N m). Torque is defined as force multiplied by perpendicular distance, which also has the SI unit Newton-meter or Joules.
questions.p: Work na force times distance, and im unit na Joule. Torque na force times perpendicular distance too, so na im get the same Joule unit.

questions.q: An electric crane lifts a load of 500 kg vertically upwards at a constant speed to a height of 12 m in 10 seconds. If the power rating of the crane is 8 kW, what is the percentage efficiency of the crane? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.e: Useful power output = (500 x 10 x 12) / 10 = 60000 / 10 = 6000 W = 6 kW. Efficiency = (Useful Power / Total Power) x 100% = (6 kW / 8 kW) x 100% = 75%.
questions.p: Calculate useful power first: (500 times 10 times 12) over 10 na 6000 Watts or 6 kW. Divide the useful power by the total power (8 kW) and multiply by 100 to get 75 percent.

questions.q: A wooden crate of mass 20 kg rests on a rough horizontal classroom floor. If the coefficient of static friction between the crate and the floor is 0.4, calculate the minimum horizontal force required to just start the crate moving. (Take acceleration due to gravity g = 10 m/s²).
questions.e: The minimum force to start motion is the maximum static friction, which is F = mu × R = mu × m × g. Substituting the values gives F = 0.4 × 20 × 10 = 80 N.
questions.p: To find the force wey go make the crate start to move, multiply coefficient of friction by normal force. That na 0.4 times 20 kg times 10 m/s², wey give us 80 N.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct concerning the coefficient of sliding friction?
o: It is independent of the normal reaction between the surfaces
It depends on the nature of the two surfaces in contact
It is always greater than the coefficient of static friction
It depends on the apparent surface area of contact between the two bodies
questions.e: The coefficient of friction depends entirely on the nature and smoothness of the two surfaces in contact. It is independent of surface area and normal reaction.
questions.p: Na the kind of material wey touch each other dey determine the coefficient of friction. Area and normal reaction no dey affect am.

questions.q: An ideal machine has a velocity ratio of 5. If an effort of 60 N is used to lift a load of 240 N, what is the percentage efficiency of the machine?
questions.e: First, find the mechanical advantage (MA = Load / Effort = 240 / 60 = 4). Then, efficiency = (MA / VR) × 100% = (4 / 5) × 100% = 80%.
questions.p: First find Mechanical Advantage by dividing load by effort to get 4. Then divide MA by Velocity Ratio (5) and multiply by 100 to get 80 percent.

questions.q: Why are ball bearings commonly used in the axles of bicycles and ceiling fans?
o: To completely eliminate all forms of friction
To increase the contact area between moving parts
To convert sliding friction into rolling friction
To increase the velocity ratio of the machine
questions.e: Rolling friction is generally much smaller than sliding friction. Ball bearings convert sliding motion into rolling motion, thereby drastically reducing frictional energy loss.
questions.p: Ball bearings dey help change sliding friction to rolling friction, and rolling friction dey small pass sliding friction. Na so dem dey reduce waste of energy.

questions.q: Which of the following methods is NOT a practical way to reduce unwanted friction in heavy industrial machinery?
o: Increasing the normal force pressing the surfaces together
Applying heavy grease or engine oil
questions.e: Increasing the normal force presses the sliding surfaces tighter together, which actually increases the frictional force rather than reducing it.
questions.p: If you increase the force wey dey press surfaces together, friction go increase join. Na so e no be method to reduce friction.

questions.q: A system of pulleys with a velocity ratio of 4 is used to lift a load of 300 N with an effort of 100 N. The work done against friction in raising the load through a height of 2 m is:
questions.e: Total work input = Effort × distance moved by effort = 100 N × (4 × 2 m) = 800 J. Useful work output = Load × height = 300 N × 2 m = 600 J. Work lost against friction = Input - Output = 800 J - 600 J = 200 J.
questions.p: Find total work input by multiplying effort by effort distance (800 J). Find useful work by multiplying load by height (600 J). Subtract output from input to get 200 J wasted for friction.

questions.q: What is the primary reason why machines can never have an efficiency of 100% in the real world?
o: The gravitational pull on the machine parts varies
Some input energy is always converted to heat due to friction
The load is always greater than the effort applied
The velocity ratio is always less than unity
questions.e: In any real machine, a fraction of the work input is always used to overcome friction between moving parts, dissipating energy as heat.
questions.p: For real life, friction must dey between parts, so small part of energy go always turn to heat. Na why machine no fit reach 100 percent.

questions.q: An inclined plane makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal. A box is pulled steadily up the plane. What is the ideal mechanical advantage of this inclined plane? (Take sin(30°) = 0.5).
questions.e: The ideal mechanical advantage of an inclined plane is given by 1 / sin(theta). Since theta = 30°, IMA = 1 / sin(30°) = 1 / 0.5 = 2.0.
questions.p: For inclined plane, Mechanical Advantage na 1 divide by sine of the angle. Since sine of 30 degree na 0.5, 1 divide by 0.5 go give you 2.

questions.q: A spiral spring of natural length 15 cm extends by 3 cm when a load of 12 N is suspended from it. What will be the total length of the spring when a load of 20 N is applied, assuming Hooke's law is obeyed?
questions.e: The extension is directly proportional to the load. For 12 N, extension is 3 cm, so 1 N gives 3/12 = 0.25 cm. For 20 N, extension = 20 × 0.25 = 5 cm, making total length 15 + 5 = 20 cm.
questions.p: As load dey increase, extension dey increase too. Since 12 N give 3 cm, 1 N go give 0.25 cm, so 20 N go give 5 cm extension. When you add am to the original 15 cm, you go get 20 cm total length.

questions.q: A metal wire obeys Hooke's law up to a tensile force of 150 N and an extension of 5.0 mm. Calculate the work done in stretching the wire from zero to this extension.
questions.e: Work done W = 0.5F × e. Substituting F = 150 N and e = 5.0 x 10⁻³ m gives W = 0.5 × 150 × 0.005 = 0.375 J.
questions.p: Work done for spring na half times force times extension (W = 0.5F × e). Change 5.0 mm to meter, multiply everything, and you go get 0.375 J.

questions.q: Two identical light springs A and B, each of force constant k, are connected in series. What is the effective force constant of the combination?
questions.e: For springs in series, the reciprocal of the effective force constant is the sum of reciprocals: 1/k_eff = 1/k + 1/k = 2/k. Therefore, k_eff = k/2 = 0.5k.
questions.p: If springs dey join for series, you go use reciprocal formula just like resistors for parallel. 1 over k_eff equal to 1/k plus 1/k, wey give you 2/k, so k_eff na half of k (0.5k).

questions.q: The energy stored in a stretched elastic string is 2.4 J when the tension is 12 N. Assuming the elastic limit is not exceeded, find the extension of the string.
questions.e: Energy E = 0.5F × e. Rearranging for extension: e = 2E / F. Substituting E = 2.4 J and F = 12 N gives e = (2 × 2.4) / 12 = 0.4 m.
questions.p: Energy wey store inside string na E = 0.5F × e. Make e subject of formula, you go get e = 2E / F. Put 2.4 J and 12 N inside, answer na 0.4 m.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about plastic deformation in solids is correct?
o: Permanent deformation occurs because the elastic limit has been exceeded
The material returns to its original shape when the load is removed
Stress is directly proportional to strain in the plastic region
Hooke's law remains valid throughout plastic deformation
questions.e: Once a material is stressed beyond its elastic limit, it undergoes plastic deformation, meaning it will not return to its original dimensions when the load is removed. Hooke's law only holds within the elastic region.
questions.p: Once you pass elastic limit, wire or material go enter plastic region. That one mean say e no go fit go back to im original shape again when you remove the load.

questions.q: A load of 50 N produces an extension of 4.0 cm on a rubber cord. What additional load is required to produce a total extension of 10.0 cm, assuming the cord obeys Hooke's law?
questions.e: Force per cm = 50 N / 4.0 cm = 12.5 N/cm. For a total extension of 10.0 cm, total force needed = 10.0 × 12.5 = 125 N. The additional load required = Total load - Initial load = 125 N - 50 N = 75 N.
questions.p: First find force per cm, wey be 50 divided by 4 to get 12.5 N/cm. Total force for 10 cm extension na 10 times 12.5, wey be 125 N. Since 50 N don dey ground before, extra load wey you need na 125 minus 50, wey be 75 N.

questions.q: What does the area under a force-extension graph for a material obeying Hooke's law represent?
questions.e: The area under a force-extension graph is calculated as 0.5Force × Extension, which represents the work done or elastic potential energy stored in the material.
questions.p: Area under force-extension graph na triangle area (half times base times height). E dey represent work done or energy wey store inside the material.

questions.q: A wooden block of mass 2.0 kg and dimensions 0.2 m x 0.1 m x 0.05 m rests on a flat table. What is the maximum pressure it can exert on the table? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.e: To get maximum pressure, the block must rest on its smallest area. Area = 0.1 m x 0.05 m = 0.005 m². Pressure = Force / Area = (2.0 x 10) / 0.005 = 20 / 0.005 = 4000 N/m².
questions.p: To get maximum pressure, make sure the area wey dey down na the smallest one. Small area na 0.1 m times 0.05 m wey be 0.005 m², con divide weight (20 N) by am to get 4000 N/m².

questions.q: A solid metal sphere weighs 50 N in air and 40 N when completely immersed in water. What is the relative density of the metal?
questions.e: Relative density is the ratio of weight in air to apparent loss of weight in water. Weight in air = 50 N, apparent loss = 50 - 40 = 10 N. Relative density = 50 / 10 = 5.0.
questions.p: Relative density na weight for air divide by how much weight drop inside water. Weight drop na 50 minus 40 wey be 10 N, so 50 divide by 10 give us 5.0.

questions.q: A hydraulic press has a small piston of cross-sectional area 4 cm² and a large piston of area 100 cm². A force of 50 N is applied to the small piston. What load can the large piston support?
questions.e: By Pascal's principle, pressure is transmitted equally: F1/A1 = F2/A2. Therefore, F2 = (F1 x A2) / A1 = (50 x 100) / 4 = 1250 N.
questions.p: Na Pascal law wey talk say pressure dey equal for both sides, so F1 over A1 equal to F2 over A2. When you cross multiply, you go get (50 times 100) divide by 4, wey be 1250 N.

questions.q: An object floats in a liquid with exactly 3/4 of its total volume submerged. Determine the density of the object if the density of the liquid is 1200 kg/m³.
questions.e: For a floating body, buoyant force equals weight: V_submerged x rho_liquid x g = V_total x rho_object x g. Thus, rho_object = (3/4) x rho_liquid = 0.75 x 1200 = 900 kg/m³.
questions.p: For object wey dey float, weight of liquid wey e displace equal to the full weight of the object. Since 3/4 of the body dey inside water, multiply 3/4 by 1200 kg/m³ to get 900 kg/m³.

questions.q: Which of the following physical quantities is measured in Pascal?
questions.e: Pressure is defined as force per unit area, and its SI unit is the Pascal (Pa), which is equivalent to N/m². The other quantities have different units.
questions.p: Pressure na force per unit area, and the correct SI unit for am na Pascal. Other options like force and momentum get different units like Newton and kg m/s.

questions.q: At what depth below the surface of a pond of water would the gauge pressure be equal to 40,000 N/m²? (Take density of water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²)
questions.e: Gauge pressure in a liquid is given by P = h x rho x g. Rearranging for depth h gives h = P / (rho x g) = 40000 / (1000 x 10) = 40000 / 10000 = 4.0 m.
questions.p: Gauge pressure formula na P = h times rho times g. Make h formula, you go divide pressure (40000) by density times gravity (10000), and answer go be 4.0 m.

questions.q: A piece of cork of volume 50 cm³ is held completely submerged in water. What is the upward buoyant force acting on it? (Density of water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²)
questions.e: Buoyant force equals the weight of the displaced water. Volume in m³ = 50 x 10⁻⁶ m³. Buoyant force = V x rho x g = 50 x 10⁻⁶ x 1000 x 10 = 0.5 N.
questions.p: Upthrust na weight of water wey the cork pack comot. Change volume to m³, then multiply volume by density and gravity (50 x 10⁻⁶ times 1000 times 10) to get 0.5 N.

questions.q: Why does a heavy iron ship float on water even though iron is much denser than water?
o: The ship is hollow, making its average density less than that of water.
The upthrust is zero because the ship moves fast.
The surface tension of water supports the weight of the ship.
The pressure at the bottom of the ship pushes it upward.
questions.e: A ship is designed with a large hollow hull filled with air, which makes the overall average density of the ship less than the density of water, allowing it to displace enough water to float.
questions.p: Ship heavy well well, but inside air plenty inside am because e hollow. Na that overall average density wey come less than water make am dey float comfortably.

questions.q: A balloon is filled with helium gas and released into the atmosphere. As it rises higher and higher into the air, what happens to the volume of the balloon?
o: It remains constant throughout its flight.
It increases because atmospheric pressure decreases.
It first increases then drops to zero instantly.
questions.e: As the helium balloon rises, atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude. According to Boyle's law, lower pressure allows the trapped gas inside to expand, causing the volume of the balloon to increase.
questions.p: As balloon dey fly go high up, pressure for air dey reduce. Because pressure reduce, the gas inside go expand according to Boyle law, make the balloon volume increase.

questions.q: Which of the following physical properties is NOT thermometric, meaning it does not vary continuously with temperature change?
o: The volume of a fixed mass of gas at constant pressure
The electrical resistance of a platinum wire
The mass of a solid block of copper
The electromotive force of a thermocouple
questions.e: A thermometric property must change measurably and continuously with temperature. The mass of a solid block of copper remains constant under normal temperature changes, whereas resistance, volume, and EMF all change with temperature.
questions.p: Na only mass of copper block no dey change as temperature dey rise. Resistance, volume and thermocouple emf dey change well well with temperature.

questions.q: A faulty mercury-in-glass thermometer reads 10 °C at the ice point and 90 °C at the steam point. What is the true temperature when this thermometer reads 50 °C?
questions.e: Using linear interpolation, T_true = ((Reading - Lower_F) / (Upper_F - Lower_F)) × 100. Substituting the values gives T_true = ((50 - 10) / (90 - 10)) × 100 = (40 / 80) × 100 = 50 °C.
questions.p: Make you use formula for faulty thermometer: (Reading minus lower faulty)/(upper faulty minus lower faulty) times 100. E go give you (50 - 10)/(90 - 10) × 100 = 50° C.

questions.q: Why does water exhibit anomalous expansion between 0 °C and 4 °C?
o: Its density increases and volume increases
Its mass decreases as it is heated
It boils faster at lower temperatures
Its volume decreases and density increases as it is heated
questions.e: Unlike most liquids that expand when heated, water contracts between 0 °C and 4 °C. This means its volume decreases while its density increases up to 4 °C.
questions.p: Instead make water expand when you heat am from 0 to 4 degree, e dey shrink. That means volume dey reduce while density dey increase.

questions.q: On a new temperature scale X, the ice point is 20 °X and the steam point is 120 °X. What temperature on the X scale corresponds to 30 °C?
questions.e: Using scale conversion: (X - 20) / (120 - 20) = (C - 0) / (100 - 0). (X - 20) / 100 = 30 / 100, which implies X - 20 = 30, so X = 50 °X.
questions.p: Make you equate the ratio for Celsius scale and new X scale: (X minus 20) over (120 minus 20) equal to 30 over 100. When you solve am, X go give you 50° X.

questions.q: Why is mercury preferred over alcohol as a thermometric liquid in clinical thermometers?
o: Mercury is transparent and requires a dye
Mercury is much cheaper and more abundant
Mercury does not wet glass and is a good conductor of heat
Mercury has a lower boiling point than alcohol
questions.e: Mercury is a good thermal conductor, expands uniformly, and does not stick (wet) to the glass walls, ensuring accurate readings unlike alcohol which wets glass.
questions.p: Mercury dey good conductor of heat, e dey expand evenly, and e no dey stick to glass wall. That's why dem prefer am pass alcohol.

questions.q: A fixed mass of gas at a constant temperature exerts a pressure of 120 kPa when its volume is 2.5 litres. What will be the new pressure if the volume is compressed to 1.0 litre?
questions.e: According to Boyle's law, P1V1 = P2V2 at constant temperature. Substituting the values gives 120 kPa × 2.5 L = P2 × 1.0 L, which yields P2 = 300 kPa.
questions.p: By Boyle law, P1V1 = P2V2 when temperature no dey change. When you put the numbers inside, 120 times 2.5 go give you P2 times 1, so P2 na 300 kPa.

questions.q: A given mass of an ideal gas occupies 400 cm³ at a temperature of 27 °C. Calculate its volume at 127 °C, assuming the pressure remains constant.
questions.e: Using Charles's law, V1/T1 = V2/T2. Temperatures must be converted to Kelvin: T1 = 300 K and T2 = 400 K, giving V2 = (400 cm³ × 400 K) / 300 K = 533.3 cm³.
questions.p: Na Charles law we go use, V1 over T1 equal V2 over T2, but make you first change temperature to Kelvin. When you calculate am well, volume 2 go come be 533 cm³.

questions.q: A student in a physics laboratory notes that the pressure of a gas inside a sealed metal cylinder is 3.0 atm at 27 °C. What will be the pressure of the gas if the cylinder is heated to 127 °C?
questions.e: According to pressure law, P1/T1 = P2/T2 at constant volume. Converting temperatures to Kelvin gives T1 = 300 K and T2 = 400 K, so P2 = (3.0 atm × 400 K) / 300 K = 4.0 atm.
questions.p: For constant volume, pressure law talk say P1 over T1 equal P2 over T2. Change Celsius to Kelvin, multiply and divide properly, you go get 4.0 atm.

questions.q: Which of the following physical quantities remains strictly constant during an isothermal process involving an ideal gas?
questions.e: An isothermal process takes place at a constant temperature. Since the internal energy of an ideal gas depends solely on its temperature, the internal energy remains unchanged.
questions.p: Isothermal process mean say temperature no dey change. Because internal energy of ideal gas dey depend only on temperature, internal energy sef no go change.

questions.q: At what temperature will the root-mean-square speed of hydrogen molecules be double their value at 27 °C, assuming ideal gas behaviour?
questions.e: RMS speed is proportional to the square root of absolute temperature (v proportional to √T). To double speed, absolute temperature must increase by a factor of 4, so T2 = 4 × 300 K = 1200 K, which is 927 °C.
questions.p: Speed dey proportional to square root of Kelvin temperature. To double the speed, temperature for Kelvin must multiply by four, meaning 1200 K, and when you minus 273, you get 927 °C.

questions.q: Which of the following assumptions is NOT part of the kinetic theory of ideal gases?
o: Intermolecular forces are negligible except during collisions
The actual volume of gas molecules is negligible compared to the container volume
Collisions between gas molecules are perfectly inelastic
Gas molecules are in continuous random motion
questions.e: Kinetic theory assumes that all collisions between gas molecules and with the container walls are perfectly elastic, meaning no kinetic energy is lost. Therefore, stating they are inelastic is incorrect.
questions.p: Kinetic theory say make molecule collision dey perfectly elastic, meaning no energy loss. So to talk say collision inelastic na lie.

questions.q: If the absolute temperature of a fixed mass of an ideal gas is halved while its volume is doubled, what happens to the pressure of the gas?
o: It increases by a factor of 4
It is reduced to a quarter of its original value
questions.e: From the ideal gas equation P = nRT/V, if T is halved (multiplied by 1/2) and V is doubled (divided by 2), the new pressure becomes P2 = (1/2) / 2P1 = (1/4) P1.
questions.p: From P equal to nRT over V, if temperature reduce by half and volume double, pressure go reduce to one-quarter of wetin e be before.

questions.q: A cylindrical vessel contains a gas at a pressure of 2.0 atm. If one-fourth of the gas leaks out while the temperature remains constant, what is the new pressure inside the vessel?
questions.e: According to the ideal gas law, pressure is directly proportional to the number of moles (P proportional to n) at constant volume and temperature. If 1/4 leaks out, 3/4 remains, so the new pressure is 3/4 × 2.0 atm = 1.5 atm.
questions.p: Pressure dey proportional to amount of gas when volume and temperature constant. If 1 quarter leak go, na 3 quarter remain, so pressure come be 1.5 atm.

questions.q: A local food vendor in Oyingbo uses an iron pot of mass 2.0 kg to boil beans. If the specific heat capacity of iron is 450 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, calculate the quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of the pot by 40° C.
questions.e: The quantity of heat is given by Q = mc Delta T. Substituting the given values, Q = 2.0 kg x 450 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ x 40 K = 36000 J.
questions.p: To find the heat, just multiply mass, specific heat capacity and temperature change together. Ebi 2.0 times 450 times 40, wey give us 36000 J.

questions.q: Which of the following physical properties is primarily responsible for the high cooling effect of water when used in automobile radiator systems?
o: High specific latent heat of vaporization
questions.e: Water has a very high specific heat capacity, allowing it to absorb a large amount of heat energy from the engine with only a small rise in its own temperature.
questions.p: Na because water get high specific heat capacity e dey make am absorb plenty heat from engine without getting too hot quick.

questions.q: An electric heater rated 1.0 kW is used to completely melt 0.5 kg of ice at 0° C. If the specific latent heat of fusion of ice is 3.3 x 10⁵ J kg⁻¹, how long does the melting process take, assuming no heat is lost to the surroundings?
questions.e: The heat required is Q = mL = 0.5 kg x 3.3 x 10⁵ J kg⁻¹ = 1.65 x 10⁵ J. Time t = Q / Power = 1.65 x 10⁵ J / 1000 W = 165 s.
questions.p: First calculate the heat to melt am using mL, then divide by power to get time. Ebi 165,000 joules divide by 1000 watts, wey give 165 seconds.

questions.q: Why does a piece of ice at 0° C cause a much more severe cooling sensation on the skin than water at 0° C?
o: Ice absorbs the specific latent heat of fusion from the skin as it melts
Water molecules move faster than ice molecules at the same temperature
Ice has a lower density than water
Ice has a higher thermal conductivity than water
questions.e: As ice melts into water at 0° C, it must absorb the specific latent heat of fusion from the skin, extracting an extra 3.34 x 10⁵ J kg⁻¹ of energy compared to water at the same temperature.
questions.p: As ice dey melt for your body, e must collect extra latent heat from your skin, making am feel colder pass ordinary water of same temperature.

questions.q: A metal block of mass 1.5 kg is heated from 25° C to 75° C. If 30 kJ of heat energy is supplied, determine the specific heat capacity of the metal.
questions.e: Using Q = mc Delta T, c = Q / (m Delta T). Here Q = 30000 J, m = 1.5 kg, Delta T = 75 - 25 = 50 K. Thus c = 30000 / (1.5 x 50) = 400 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.
questions.p: Make c the subject of formula: c = Q over m times Delta T. Ebi 30000 divide by (1.5 times 50), wey give 400.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about specific latent heat is correct?
o: It depends on the mass of the substance undergoing a phase change
It only applies to substances changing from liquid to gas
It is the quantity of heat required to change the temperature of unit mass by 1 K
It is the quantity of heat required to change unit mass of a substance from solid to liquid without temperature change
questions.e: Specific latent heat is defined as the thermal energy required to change the phase of 1 kg of a substance without any change in its temperature.
questions.p: Specific latent heat na the heat wey 1 kg of substance need to change state without any change in temperature o.

questions.q: Equal masses of water and a certain liquid are supplied with the same quantity of heat. If the temperature of the liquid rises three times as much as that of water, what is the specific heat capacity of the liquid, given that the specific heat capacity of water is 4200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹?
questions.e: Since Q = m c_w Delta T_w = m c_l Delta T_l and Delta T_l = 3 Delta T_w, we have c_w Delta T_w = c_l (3 Delta T_w). Therefore, c_l = c_w / 3 = 4200 / 3 = 1400 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.
questions.p: Since heat energy equal, temperature change and specific heat capacity dey inversely proportional. Liquid temperature rise 3 times, meaning hin capacity na water capacity divide by 3, wey be 1400.

questions.q: Which of the following modes of heat transfer does NOT require a material medium for its propagation?
questions.e: Radiation transfers heat through electromagnetic waves and can travel through a complete vacuum without needing any medium. Conduction and convection both require particles of a solid, liquid, or gas to transfer heat.
questions.p: Radiation dey carry heat through space without need any material or air. Conduction and convection must get particles before dem fit transfer heat.

questions.q: During a sunny afternoon in Owerri, Mr. Emeka observed that the corrugated iron roof of his bungalow became very hot. Which process was mainly responsible for transferring heat from the sun to the roof?
questions.e: Heat from the sun reaches the Earth through space by infrared radiation, as there is a vacuum between the sun and the Earth's atmosphere.
questions.p: Heat from sun dey reach us through space by radiation because empty space dey between sun and Earth.

questions.q: A metal rod of length 2.0 m has one end placed in a glowing charcoal fire while the other end is held. The temperature of the hot end is 100° C and the cold end is 20° C. The cross-sectional area of the rod is 5.0 x 10⁻⁴ m² and its thermal conductivity is 200 W/(m·K). What is the rate of heat flow along the rod?
questions.e: Using the rate of heat transfer formula Q/t = k × A × (T1 - T2) / L. Substituting the given values: (200 × 5.0 x 10⁻⁴ × (100 - 20)) / 2.0 = 4.0 W.
questions.p: We use the formula Q/t = kA(T1 - T2)/L. Put the numbers inside: (200 × 5e-4 × 80) / 2, and you go get 4.0 W.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about convection in fluids is correct?
o: It occurs rapidly in solids due to free electrons.
It involves the actual movement of heated fluid molecules.
It can take place efficiently in a complete vacuum.
It is primarily caused by electromagnetic waves.
questions.e: Convection happens in liquids and gases where warmer, less dense fluid rises and cooler, denser fluid sinks, causing bulk movement of the fluid.
questions.p: Convection dey happen when hot liquid or gas wey light dey rise up, and cold heavy one dey come down.

questions.q: A double-glazed glass window consists of two glass panes separated by a trapped layer of dry air. This design primarily reduces heat transfer through the window by minimizing which two processes?
questions.e: Trapped air is a poor conductor of heat, which minimizes conduction. The narrow gap also restricts the circulation of air, which greatly reduces convection currents.
questions.p: Trapped air no good to conduct heat, so conduction reduce. The space tight well well, so air no fit move anyhow to do convection.

questions.q: Why are kettle handles in many Nigerian kitchens often made of plastic or wood rather than pure copper or aluminum?
o: Plastics and wood have very high thermal conductivity.
Plastics and wood are excellent emitters of radiant heat.
Plastics and wood allow quick convection currents.
Plastics and wood have very low thermal conductivity.
questions.e: Kettle handles need to remain cool to the touch when the water inside is boiling, so they are made of materials with very low thermal conductivity like wood or plastic to prevent heat conduction to the hand.
questions.p: Make your hand no burn when water don boil, dem dey use wood or plastic because dem no dey allow heat to pass through them easily.

questions.q: Two identical metal spheres, one painted dull black and the other highly polished, are heated to the same high temperature of 400° C and left to cool in a vacuum chamber at room temperature. Which sphere cools down faster and why?
o: The polished sphere, because it is a better reflector of heat.
The black sphere, because a dull black surface is a good emitter of radiation.
The polished sphere, because smooth surfaces conduct heat better.
Both spheres cool at the exact same rate in a vacuum.
questions.e: A dull black surface is a very good absorber and emitter of radiant heat compared to a shiny polished surface, causing it to lose heat by radiation much faster.
questions.p: Black surface be good emitter of heat, so the black sphere go cool down quick quick pass the shining polished one.

questions.q: A transverse wave travelling along a stretched string has a frequency of 50 Hz and a wavelength of 0.4 m. Calculate the speed of the wave.
questions.e: The speed of a wave is given by the product of its frequency and wavelength, v = f × lambda. Substituting the given values, v = 50 Hz × 0.4 m = 20.0 m/s.
questions.p: To find wave speed, multiply frequency by wavelength. Na 50 times 0.4 we go do, e go give us 20 m/s.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes between longitudinal and transverse waves?
o: Transverse waves consist of alternate crests and troughs while longitudinal consist of compressions and rarefactions
Longitudinal waves require a material medium while transverse waves do not require any medium at all
Transverse wave particles vibrate parallel to wave travel while longitudinal do so perpendicularly
Longitudinal waves can be polarised while transverse waves cannot
questions.e: Transverse waves travel through crests and troughs where particle motion is perpendicular to wave propagation, whereas longitudinal waves travel through compressions and rarefactions where particle motion is parallel.
questions.p: Transverse wave get crest and trough, and dem dey move up and down perpendicular to the wave direction. Longitudinal wave own na compression and rarefaction.

questions.q: A sound wave passes from air into water. Which of the following wave properties remains completely unchanged?
questions.e: When a wave travels from one medium to another, its frequency remains constant because it is determined by the source. However, speed and wavelength change, and amplitude usually decreases due to partial reflection.
questions.p: When wave cross from one medium enter another one, frequency no dey change at all because na the source dey control am. Na only speed and wavelength dey change.

questions.q: Two in-phase wave sources produce ripples on a pond's surface. At a certain point, the path difference from the two sources to the point is 3.5 wavelengths. What type of interference occurs at this point?
questions.e: A path difference of 3.5 wavelengths (which is an odd multiple of half a wavelength, (2n + 1) × lambda / 2) leads to destructive interference because the waves arrive completely out of phase.
questions.p: If path difference be odd number of half-wavelength like 3.5 lambda, the waves go cancel each other out, and na destructive interference be that.

questions.q: A stationary wave is set up on a stretched string of length 1.5 m fixed at both ends vibrating in its fundamental mode. If the speed of transverse waves on the string is 300 m/s, determine the fundamental frequency of the string.
questions.e: For a string fixed at both ends, the fundamental wavelength is lambda = 2L = 2 × 1.5 m = 3.0 m. The frequency is f = v / lambda = 300 m/s / 3.0 m = 100 Hz.
questions.p: For string wey dem bind for both ends, fundamental wavelength na twice the length, wey be 3 meters. Divide speed by wavelength to get frequency: 300 divide by 3 na 100 Hz.

questions.q: Which of the following phenomena is exclusively exhibited by transverse waves and provides proof that light is a transverse wave?
questions.e: Polarisation restricts the oscillation of wave particles to a single plane and only occurs in transverse waves. Light undergoes polarisation, proving its transverse nature.
questions.p: Na only transverse wave fit undergo polarisation because na only dem get side-to-side vibration wey man fit block with polaroid filter.

questions.q: An echo sounder on a Nigerian naval patrol boat emits an ultrasonic wave towards the seabed and receives the reflected signal 0.8 seconds later. If the speed of sound in seawater is 1500 m/s, calculate the depth of the seabed.
questions.e: The total distance travelled by the wave is 2depth = v × t = 1500 m/s × 0.8 s = 1200 m. Therefore, the depth is 1200 / 2 = 600 m.
questions.p: Sound go go bottom and come back, so we must multiply speed by time and divide result by 2. Na 1500 times 0.8 divide by 2, wey give us 600 meters.

questions.q: A radio station in Abuja broadcasts at a frequency of 100 MHz. Given that the speed of electromagnetic waves in air is 3 × 10⁸ m/s, what is the wavelength of the broadcast signal?
questions.e: Using the wave equation c = f × lambda, lambda = c / f. Substituting values: lambda = (3 × 10⁸) / (100 × 10⁶) = 300 × 10⁶ / 100 × 10⁶ = 3.0 m.
questions.p: Use wave formula lambda = c over f. Divide 3 times 10 power 8 by 100 million Hz, you go get 3 meters.

questions.q: When a wave enters a shallow region from a deep region in a ripple tank, which of the following changes is observed?
o: Wavelength increases and frequency remains constant
questions.e: In shallow water, wave speed decreases. Since frequency remains constant (determined by the generator), the wavelength must also decrease according to v = f × lambda.
questions.p: As wave enter shallow water, speed dey drop. Since frequency constant, wavelength must reduce too because speed and wavelength dey follow each other.

questions.q: A sound wave travels through air at a speed of 340 m/s with a frequency of 170 Hz. What is the wavelength of this sound wave?
questions.e: The wavelength is calculated using the wave equation v = f × lambda, where v is speed and f is frequency. Substituting the values gives lambda = 340 / 170 = 2.0 m.
questions.p: To find wavelength, divide the speed by the frequency. When you divide 340 by 170, you go get 2.0 metres.

questions.q: Which of the following physical properties is primarily responsible for the different pitch heard from a talking drum compared to a wooden gong?
questions.e: Pitch is the psychological attribute of sound that directly depends on its frequency. Higher frequency produces a higher pitch, while lower frequency produces a lower pitch.
questions.p: Na frequency dey determine whether sound go high pitch or low pitch. As frequency increase, pitch dey high.

questions.q: An open pipe of length 50 cm produces its fundamental note in air. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, what is the frequency of this fundamental note?
questions.e: For an open pipe, the fundamental wavelength is lambda = 2L = 2 × 0.5 = 1.0 m. The frequency is f = v / lambda = 340 / 1.0 = 340 Hz.
questions.p: For open pipe, wavelength na twice the length, wey be 1.0 m. Divide speed 340 by wavelength 1.0 to get 340 Hz.

questions.q: A student claps her hands in front of a tall cliff at Ibadan and hears the echo 1.5 seconds later. If the speed of sound is 330 m/s, how far is the student from the cliff?
questions.e: The sound travels to the cliff and back, covering distance 2d = v × t. Therefore, d = (330 × 1.5) / 2 = 247.5 m.
questions.p: As sound go go and come back, make you multiply speed by time, then divide by two. 330 times 1.5 divided by 2 na 247.5 metres.

questions.q: A closed organ pipe has a length of 25 cm. Given that the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, what is the frequency of its first overtone (third harmonic)?
questions.e: For a closed pipe, the frequencies are odd harmonics: f_n = n × v / (4L) for n = 1, 3, 5... The first overtone is the third harmonic (n = 3). Thus, f_3 = 3 × 340 / (4 × 0.25) = 1020 Hz.
questions.p: For closed pipe, na only odd harmonics dey show, so first overtone na third harmonic. Use formula f = 3v / (4L) to get 1020 Hz.

questions.q: Why do sound waves travel faster in humid air than in dry air at the same temperature?
o: Water molecules have a lower molar mass than diatomic oxygen and nitrogen molecules
Water vapour increases the density of air significantly
Humidity decreases the elasticity of the air medium
Sound waves undergo less refraction in wet air
questions.e: Humid air contains water vapour (H2O, molar mass 18 g/mol), which replaces heavier N2 (28 g/mol) and O2 (32 g/mol) molecules. A lower average molar mass at the same temperature increases the root-mean-square speed of gas molecules, hence increasing sound speed.
questions.p: Water vapour lighter pass nitrogen and oxygen inside air. When air humid, the average weight reduce, make sound travel faster.

questions.q: Which of the following phenomena is solely responsible for the reinforcement or cancellation of sound when two waves of identical frequency superimpose?
questions.e: Interference is the superposition of two or more waves resulting in a new wave pattern of constructive (reinforcement) or destructive (cancellation) combination.
questions.p: Na interference happen when two sound waves jam together to make sound loud or quiet.

questions.q: A resonance tube experiment is performed using a tuning fork of frequency 425 Hz. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, at what shortest length of the air column will resonance occur?
questions.e: The shortest length for resonance in a closed tube is L = lambda / 4. First find lambda = v / f = 340 / 425 = 0.8 m. Then L = 0.8 / 4 = 0.2 m, which is 20 cm.
questions.p: Shortest length na quarter of wavelength. Find wavelength first by doing 340 / 425, then divide by 4 to get 0.2 m or 20 cm.

questions.q: A ray of light is incident on a smooth plane mirror at an angle of 35° to the reflecting surface. What is the angle of reflection?
questions.e: The angle of incidence is measured between the incident ray and the normal (perpendicular) to the surface. Since the angle with the surface is 35°, the angle of incidence is 90° - 35° = 55°. By the laws of reflection, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, which is 55°.
questions.p: Na angle betaween incident ray and normal we dey use as angle of incidence. Since the surface angle na 35°, angle of incidence go be 90 minus 35, wey be 55°. Di law of reflection talk say angle of reflection must equal angle of incidence, so na 55°.

questions.q: A concave mirror produces a real image three times the size of the object. If the object distance is 12 cm, what is the focal length of the mirror?
questions.e: The linear magnification m = v/u = 3, so v = 3u = 3(12) = 36 cm. For a real image formed by a concave mirror, v and u are both positive in magnitude terms for formula substitution, so 1/f = 1/12 + 1/36 = 4/36 = 1/9, giving f = 9 cm.
questions.p: Magnification m = v/u = 3, meaning v = 3 times 12 wey be 36 cm. Put am inside 1/f = 1/u + 1/v, we get 1/f = 1/12 + 1/36, wey give us f = 9 cm.

questions.q: Two plane mirrors are inclined at an angle of 60° to each other. How many images of an object placed symmetrically between them will be formed?
questions.e: The number of images n is given by the formula (360 / theta) - 1. Since theta = 60°, n = (360 / 60) - 1 = 6 - 1 = 5 images.
questions.p: Di formula for number of images na (360 / theta) minus 1. Since angle na 60°, we divide 360 by 60 to get 6, then minus 1 to get 5 images.

questions.q: Which of the following characteristics is NOT associated with the image formed by a convex mirror for any real object position?
questions.e: A convex mirror always produces images that are virtual, diminished, and erect for all real object positions. It can never form an inverted image because the reflected rays diverge.
questions.p: Convex mirror dey always give you virtual, small (diminished), and upright (erect) image for any real object. E no dey ever form inverted image because di rays dey scatter (diverge).

questions.q: An object stands 4 cm tall in front of a convex mirror of radius of curvature 20 cm. If the object is 10 cm away from the mirror, what is the height of the image?
questions.e: Focal length f = -20/2 = -10 cm. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives -1/10 = 1/10 + 1/v, so v = -5 cm. Magnification m = height of image / height of object = -v/u = -(-5)/10 = 0.5. Thus, image height = 0.5 × 4 cm = 2.0 cm.
questions.p: First find focal length f = -20/2 = -10 cm. Use mirror formula find v, wey come be -5 cm. Magnification na -v/u = 0.5. Multiply am with object height 4 cm, you go get 2.0 cm.

questions.q: A boy stands 2 m away from a large vertical plane mirror. If he walks 0.5 m towards the mirror, what is the new distance between the boy and his image?
questions.e: Initially, object distance equals image distance (2 m), so total distance between boy and image is 4 m. When he walks 0.5 m towards the mirror, his new distance from the mirror is 2 - 0.5 = 1.5 m. His image is also 1.5 m behind the mirror, making the total distance between him and his image 1.5 m + 1.5 m = 3.0 m.
questions.p: Before, boy and im image distance na 2m plus 2m = 4m. When im waka 0.5m come front, im new distance to mirror na 1.5m. Im image dey 1.5m inside mirror too, so distance bwin dem two na 1.5m + 1.5m = 3.0m.

questions.q: Why are parabolic mirrors preferred over spherical mirrors for large astronomical telescopes?
questions.e: Parabolic mirrors converge all parallel rays coming from distant stars to a single sharp focal point, thereby eliminating spherical aberration which plagues spherical mirrors.
questions.p: Parabolic mirror dey gather all straight rays from star go one single sharp point. E dey remove that blur-blur error wey spherical mirror dey bring, wey dem dey call spherical aberration.

questions.q: Light travels from air into a transparent palm oil block with an absolute refractive index of 1.5. If the angle of incidence in air is 60°, what is the sine of the angle of refraction in the palm oil? (Take sin 60° as 0.8660)
questions.e: Using Snell's law, n = sin(i) / sin(r), so sin(r) = sin(60) / 1.5. Substituting the values gives 0.8660 / 1.5 = 0.5773.
questions.p: Make you apply Snell law, n = sin(i) / sin(r). If you divide 0.8660 by 1.5, you go get 0.5773.

questions.q: What is the critical angle for a glass-air boundary if the refractive index of the glass is 1.414?
questions.e: The critical angle c is given by sin(c) = 1 / n. Therefore, sin(c) = 1 / 1.414 = 0.7071, which means c = 45°.
questions.p: To find critical angle, use sin(c) = 1 / n. When you divide 1 by 1.414, you get 0.7071, and sin of 45° give that one.

questions.q: An object is placed 20 cm in front of a thin convex lens of focal length 10 cm. What is the distance of the image formed from the lens?
questions.e: Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/u + 1/v, we have 1/10 = 1/20 + 1/v. This gives 1/v = 1/10 - 1/20 = 1/20, so v = 20 cm.
questions.p: Use lens formula 1/f = 1/u + 1/v. If you put 1/10 minus 1/20, na 1/20 remain, meaning v na 20 cm.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best explains why a swimming pool appears shallower than its actual depth?
o: Total internal reflection of light at the water surface
Interference of light waves reflected from the pool floor
Diffraction of light waves around the edges of the pool
Refraction of light rays as they pass from water into the air
questions.e: Light rays coming from the bottom of the pool bend away from the normal as they enter the less dense air, making the image appear closer to the surface.
questions.p: As light dey leave water enter air, e dey bend away from normal. Na dis bending make the pool floor look higher than e actually dey.

questions.q: What name is given to the phenomenon where white light passing through a triangular glass prism splits into its component colors?
questions.e: Dispersion is the splitting of white light into different colors due to varying refractive indices for different wavelengths in the medium.
questions.p: Dispersion mean when white light scatter into different rainbow colors because each color travel with different speed inside glass.

questions.q: An optical fiber transmits light efficiently because the core has a refractive index that is...
o: equal to the cladding, causing zero refraction
higher than the cladding, causing total internal reflection
lower than the cladding, causing total internal reflection
zero, preventing any absorption of light energy
questions.e: An optical fiber works on total internal reflection, which requires the inner core to have a higher optical density (higher refractive index) than the outer cladding.
questions.p: Optical fiber dey work based on total internal reflection. Core must get higher refractive index pass cladding so light go bounce inside.

questions.q: A converging lens has a power of +5.0 Diopters. What is the focal length of this lens in meters?
questions.e: Power of a lens is P = 1 / f (where f is in meters). Thus, f = 1 / 5.0 = 0.20 m.
questions.p: Power na reciprocal of focal length in meters, so P = 1 / f. If P na 5.0, f na 1 / 5 which be 0.20 m.

questions.q: Two identical metal spheres carry charges of +4 micro-Coulombs and -8 micro-Coulombs respectively. When they are brought into contact and then separated to a distance, what is the final charge on each sphere?
questions.e: When identical spheres touch, total charge is conserved and shared equally. Total charge = (+4 micro-C) + (-8 micro-C) = -4 micro-C, so each gets -4 / 2 = -2 micro-C.
questions.p: When identical balls touch, you go add di charges together and divide am by two. Di total charge na -4, so when you share am into two, each person go get -2 micro-coulomb.

questions.q: Which of the following describes an equipotential surface around an isolated point charge in a vacuum?
o: A hollow cylinder surrounding the electric field
A series of concentric spheres centred on the charge
A set of parallel lines radiating outwards from the charge
A flat plane perpendicular to the electric field lines
questions.e: An equipotential surface has the same electric potential everywhere. For an isolated point charge, potential depends only on distance r, forming concentric spherical shells.
questions.p: Equipotential surface mean everywhere for di surface get same potential. For one single point charge, na circle for 3D, wey be concentric spheres wey surround di charge.

questions.q: Three capacitors of values 2 micro-F, 3 micro-F and 6 micro-F are connected in series. Calculate their equivalent capacitance.
questions.e: For series connection: 1/C_eq = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = (3 + 2 + 1)/6 = 6/6 = 1. Therefore, C_eq = 1 micro-F.
questions.p: For series capacitor, you go use reciprocal formula. 1 over 2 plus 1 over 3 plus 1 over 6 go give you 1 over 1, so total capacitance na 1 micro-farad.

questions.q: What is the electrostatic potential energy stored in a 4 micro-F capacitor when it is charged to a potential difference of 100 Volts?
questions.p: Energy wey capacitor hold na half times capacitance times voltage squared. When you calculate 0.5 times 4 times 10 power minus 6 times 100 squared, you go get 0.02 Joules.

questions.q: An uncharged metal sphere is connected to the Earth while a positively charged rod is brought close to it without touching. What happens when the Earth connection is broken first, and then the rod is removed?
o: The sphere acquires a negative charge
The sphere becomes a permanent magnet
The sphere acquires a positive charge
questions.e: The positive rod attracts electrons from the Earth into the sphere. Breaking the earth connection traps these extra electrons, leaving the sphere negatively charged after the rod is removed.
questions.p: When you bring positive rod near, electrons go flow enter di sphere from ground. If you remove ground wire first, di electrons go remain trapped, making di sphere get negative charge.

questions.q: Which of the following materials is most suitable to be used as a dielectric inside a high-performance capacitor?
questions.e: A dielectric must be an electrical insulator with high breakdown voltage. Mica is a well-known insulating material used extensively in capacitors.
questions.p: Dielectric must be insulator wey no dey allow current to pass easily. Mica na very good insulator wey dem dey use inside capacitor.

questions.q: A dry cell of e.m.f. 1.5 V and internal resistance 0.5 ohms is connected across an external resistor of 2.5 ohms. What is the terminal potential difference across the cell?
questions.e: First find the circuit current: I = E / (R + r) = 1.5 / (2.5 + 0.5) = 0.5 A. The terminal potential difference is V = I × R = 0.5 × 2.5 = 1.25 V.
questions.p: Make you find current first: I = 1.5 divide by (2.5 + 0.5) wey give 0.5 A. Na im make terminal voltage V = 0.5 multiply by 2.5, wey be 1.25 V.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about Ohm's law is correct for a metallic conductor at constant temperature?
o: Potential difference is inversely proportional to the resistance
Current is directly proportional to the applied potential difference
Current is inversely proportional to the applied potential difference
Resistance is directly proportional to the current flowing through it
questions.e: Ohm's law states that the current flowing through a metallic conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends, provided physical conditions like temperature remain constant.
questions.p: Ohm law talk say current wey dey flow for wire dey follow body-body with voltage, as long as temperature no change.

questions.q: Three resistors of values 2 ohms, 3 ohms, and 6 ohms are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance of the combination?
questions.e: For parallel resistors, 1/R = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = (3 + 2 + 1)/6 = 6/6 = 1 ohm⁻¹. Therefore, R = 1 / 1 = 1.0 ohm.
questions.p: If resistors dey parallel, you go add inverse: 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 6/6 = 1. When you turn am upside down, R still remain 1 ohm.

questions.q: A storage battery has an e.m.f. of 12 V. When a current of 3 A is drawn from it, the terminal voltage drops to 10.5 V. Calculate the internal resistance of the battery.
questions.e: Using the relation E = V + Ir, rearrange for r: r = (E - V) / I = (12 - 10.5) / 3 = 1.5 / 3 = 0.5 ohm.
questions.p: Use formula E = V + Ir. Bring out r: r = (12 minus 10.5) divide by 3, wey give you 0.5 ohm.

questions.q: A network consists of a 4-ohm resistor connected in series with a parallel combination of two 6-ohm resistors. What is the total resistance of the network?
questions.e: The parallel combination of two 6-ohm resistors gives R_p = (6 × 6) / (6 + 6) = 3 ohms. Adding the 4-ohm resistor in series gives R_total = 4 + 3 = 7.0 ohms.
questions.p: First solve the two 6 ohm wey dey parallel, e go give you 3 ohm. Then add am to the 4 ohm wey dey series, na 7 ohm you go get.

questions.q: What is the primary function of internal resistance in a real source of electromotive force?
o: To increase the total current delivered to an external circuit
To prevent short circuits across the battery terminals
To maintain a constant potential difference regardless of load
To cause a drop in terminal voltage when current flows
questions.e: Internal resistance represents the opposition offered by the materials inside the cell itself. As current flows, it causes a potential drop (Ir) inside the source, reducing the available terminal voltage.
questions.p: Internal resistance na the wahala wey dey inside battery body. Once current dey flow, e dey cause voltage drop so terminal voltage go reduce.

questions.q: Two identical cells, each of e.m.f. 2.0 V and internal resistance 1.0 ohm, are connected in parallel across a 0.5-ohm external resistor. Find the current flowing through the external resistor.
questions.e: For two identical cells in parallel, effective e.m.f. E = 2.0 V, and effective internal resistance r = 1.0 / 2 = 0.5 ohm. Current I = E / (R + r) = 2.0 / (0.5 + 0.5) = 2.0 A.
questions.p: If two same cells join parallel, voltage still remain 2 V, but internal resistance come down to 0.5 ohm. Current na 2 divide by (0.5 + 0.5) wey be 2 A.

questions.q: A student sets up a circuit with a variable resistor connected to a DC generator of constant e.m.f. As the resistance of the variable resistor is decreased towards zero, what happens to the current and the terminal p.d.?
o: Current remains constant and terminal p.d. decreases
Current increases and terminal p.d. approaches zero
Current increases and terminal p.d. increases
Current decreases and terminal p.d. increases
questions.e: As R decreases, I = E / (R + r) increases significantly. Since terminal p.d. is V = E - Ir, a larger current causes a larger internal drop, making V drop towards zero.
