questions.p: As resistance reduce, current go shoot up. Because current high, the voltage loss inside battery go plenty, make terminal voltage come crash reach zero.

questions.q: In an experiment to determine e.m.f. and internal resistance, a potentiometer gives a balance length of 75.0 cm on an open circuit, and 60.0 cm when a 4.0-ohm resistor is connected across the cell. Calculate the internal resistance of the cell.
questions.p: Use potentiometer formula: r = R times (L1 minus L2) divide by L2. Na im be 4 multiply by 15 divide by 60, wey give you 1 ohm flat.

questions.q: Calculate the electrical power dissipated in a heating element connected to a 240 V mains supply if it draws a steady current of 5 A.
questions.e: Electrical power P is calculated using the formula P = IV. Substituting the values, P = 5 A × 240 V = 1200 W.
questions.p: To find power, multiply current by voltage. Dat na 5 times 240, wey give us 1200 W.

questions.q: An electric pressing iron operates on a 220 V supply and draws a current of 4 A. Determine the energy consumed in kilowatt-hours (kWh) if the iron is used for 3 hours.
questions.e: Power P = IV = 220 × 4 = 880 W = 0.88 kW. Energy E = P × t = 0.88 kW × 3 hours = 2.64 kWh.
questions.p: First find power in kilowatts by multiplying 220 by 4 and dividing by 1000 to get 0.88 kW. Then multiply by 3 hours to get 2.64 kWh.

questions.q: A consumer uses a 2 kW water heater for 2 hours daily for a period of 30 days. If the cost of electrical energy is ₦50 per kWh, calculate the total cost of electricity consumed.
questions.e: Total energy = Power × time × days = 2 kW × 2 hours/day × 30 days = 120 kWh. Total cost = 120 kWh × ₦50/kWh = ₦6,000.
questions.p: Total energy na 2 kW times 2 hours times 30 days, wey be 120 kWh. Multiply am by ₦50 to get ₦6,000.

questions.q: Which of the following units is equivalent to the kilowatt-hour (kWh)?
questions.e: The kilowatt-hour is a unit of electrical energy, and energy is measured in Joules. One kilowatt-hour equals 3.6 million Joules.
questions.p: Kilowatt-hour na unit for energy, and energy unit for SI system na Joule.

questions.q: A 100 W lamp is left switched on continuously for 5 days in a school laboratory. Determine the total electrical energy consumed in Joules.
questions.e: Power = 100 W. Time in seconds = 5 days × 24 hours/day × 3600 seconds/hour = 432,000 s. Energy = P × t = 100 × 432,000 = 4.32 × 10⁷ J.
questions.p: Change 5 days to seconds first (5 × 24 × 3600 = 432,000 s). Then multiply by power 100 W to get 4.32 × 10⁷ Joules.

questions.q: An electric appliance with a resistance of 40 ohms is connected to a 200 V source. What is the rate at which heat is generated in the appliance?
questions.e: Power P = V² / R. Substituting the values, P = (200²) / 40 = 40000 / 40 = 1000 W.
questions.p: Use formula P = V-square over R. Dat na 200 times 200 divided by 40, wey give us 1000 W.

questions.q: Why are electrical transmission lines operated at very high voltages and low currents over long distances?
o: To increase the current reaching the consumers
To make the electricity travel faster
To increase the resistance of the cables
To reduce power loss due to heating in the cables
questions.e: Power loss in transmission cables is given by P = I² R. By stepping up voltage, current I is significantly reduced, which drastically minimizes the I² R power losses.
questions.p: High voltage reduce current inside wire. Since heat loss na I-square R, small current mean say small power go waste as heat.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a fuse in a domestic electrical circuit?
o: To store electrical energy for emergency use
To melt and break the circuit when current exceeds a safe limit
To step up the mains voltage
To regulate the flow of alternating current
questions.e: A fuse contains a thin wire with a low melting point that melts and opens the circuit if the current becomes dangerously high, preventing damage or fire.
questions.p: Fuse wire dey melt quick when too much current pass, so e go break circuit to protect appliances from burning.

questions.q: An electric kettle is rated 2.5 kW, 250 V. Calculate the current drawn by the kettle when operating normally.
questions.e: Using P = IV, we have I = P / V. Converting power to watts, P = 2500 W. Thus, I = 2500 / 250 = 10 A.
questions.p: Make you use I = P over V. Convert 2.5 kW to 2500 W, then divide by 250 V to get 10 A.

questions.q: Which of the following materials is classified as diamagnetic?
questions.e: Copper is weakly repelled by a magnetic field, making it diamagnetic. Iron, cobalt, and nickel are strongly ferromagnetic.
questions.p: Copper na diamagnetic metal because magnetic field dey push am small. Iron, cobalt and nickel na ferromagnetic materials.

questions.q: A straight current-carrying conductor of length 0.5 m is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of flux density 0.4 T. If a current of 3 A flows through the conductor, what is the magnitude of the magnetic force experienced by it?
questions.e: The magnetic force is given by F = I L B sin(theta). Substituting the values: F = 3 A × 0.5 m × 0.4 T × sin(90°) = 0.6 N.
questions.p: To find magnetic force, use formula F = I L B sin(theta). When you multiply 3 times 0.5 times 0.4, you go get 0.6 N.

questions.q: Lenz's law of electromagnetic induction is a direct consequence of the law of conservation of:
questions.e: Lenz's law states that the induced current opposes the change causing it, which ensures that energy is conserved during induction.
questions.p: Lenz law talk say the current wey dem induce go fight the change wey bring am, and na conservation of energy make am happen.

questions.q: A transformer has 400 turns in its primary coil and 80 turns in its secondary coil. If an alternating voltage of 220 V is applied to the primary, what is the output voltage in the secondary?
questions.e: Using the transformer turns ratio equation, Vs / Vp = Ns / Np. Thus, Vs = (80 / 400) × 220 V = 44 V.
questions.p: Use transformer formula Vs equals Ns over Np times Vp. When you calculate 80 divide by 400 multiply by 220, answer na 44 V.

questions.q: Which of the following devices works purely on the principle of electromagnetic induction?
questions.e: An induction coil uses mutual induction to step up DC voltage into high voltage sparks. The others operate on heating effects, magnetic force on conductors, or resistance variation.
questions.p: Na induction coil dey use electromagnetic induction well well to produce high voltage spark. The other devices dey use different principles like heat or motor effect.

questions.q: A circular coil of 50 turns and radius 0.1 m is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T normal to the coil. If the field drops to zero in 0.05 s, calculate the magnitude of the induced electromotive force in the coil. (Take π = 3.14)
questions.e: Area A = π × r² = 3.14(0.1)² = 0.0314 m². Initial flux = N × B × A = 50 × 0.2 × 0.0314 = 0.314 Wb. Induced emf = Delta(flux) / time = 0.314 / 0.05 = 6.28 V.
questions.p: First find area using π r square, then calculate total magnetic flux linkage. Divide change in flux by time 0.05 s to get 6.28 V.

questions.q: The angle between the earth's magnetic field and the horizontal component of the earth's magnetic field at a given location is called the angle of:
questions.e: The angle of dip (or magnetic inclination) is the angle that the total magnetic field of the Earth makes with the horizontal plane.
questions.p: The angle wey earth magnetic field make with ground level na wetin we dey call angle of dip.

questions.q: A bar magnet is broken into two equal pieces perpendicular to its length. Each new piece will:
o: become a monopole with only a north pole
become a monopole with only a south pole
have both a north and a south pole
questions.e: Magnetic monopoles do not exist; whenever a magnet is broken, each piece immediately forms its own north and south poles.
questions.p: Magnetic pole no dey stay single. If you break magnet into two, each small piece go still get north and south pole.

questions.q: In a step-down transformer, energy losses due to eddy currents in the soft iron core are minimized by:
questions.e: Laminating the soft iron core introduces thin layers of insulation that break up the path of eddy currents, thereby reducing heat loss.
questions.p: To stop eddy currents from wasting power as heat, engineers dey laminate the iron core into thin sheets with insulation.

questions.q: A particle executing simple harmonic motion has a maximum displacement of 0.05 m and a maximum speed of 3.14 m/s. What is the frequency of the oscillation? (Take π = 3.14)
questions.e: Maximum speed in SHM is given by v_max = 2pi × f × A. Substituting the values gives 3.14 = 2 × 3.14f × 0.05, which simplifies to f = 10.0 Hz.
questions.p: Maximum speed for SHM na v_max = 2pi × f × A. When you put inside the numbers, 3.14 = 2 × 3.14f × 0.05, you go get f = 10.0 Hz.

questions.q: Which of the following physical quantities remains constant throughout the motion of an ideal simple pendulum oscillating with small amplitude?
questions.e: In an ideal pendulum without friction, energy is conserved between kinetic and potential forms. Therefore, the total mechanical energy remains constant throughout the motion.
questions.p: For ideal pendulum wey no get friction, energy dey change between kinetic and potential. But the total mechanical energy dey remain constant all through.

questions.q: The displacement x of a body executing simple harmonic motion is given by x = 0.4 sin(50t), where x is in meters and t in seconds. What is the maximum acceleration of the body?
questions.e: Comparing x = A sin(omega × t), the amplitude A = 0.4 m and angular frequency omega = 50 rad/s. Maximum acceleration is a_max = omega² × A = (50²) × 0.4 = 1000 m/s².
questions.p: If you compare with x = A sin(omega × t), amplitude A = 0.4 and omega = 50. Maximum acceleration na omega² × A, so 50 square times 0.4 go give you 1000 m/s².

questions.q: What happens to the period of a simple pendulum if its length is increased by a factor of 4?
o: It increases by a factor of 4
questions.e: The period T is directly proportional to the square root of the length (T proportional to √L). If L is multiplied by 4, T is multiplied by √4, which is 2.
questions.p: Period T dey proportional to square root of length L. If you multiply L by 4, T go multiply by square root of 4, meaning e go double.

questions.q: A mass of 2 kg attached to a light spring executes simple harmonic motion with a period of 0.5 s. What is the force constant (stiffness) of the spring? (Take π = 3.14)
questions.e: The period of a mass-spring system is T = 2pi × √(m / k). Rearranging for k gives k = 4pi² × m / T². Substituting m = 2 kg and T = 0.5 s gives k = 4(3.14²) × 2 / (0.5²) = 315.6 N/m.
questions.p: For mass-spring system, T = 2pi × √(m / k). When you arrange am for k, k = 4pi² × m / T². Put m = 2 and T = 0.5, you go get 315.6 N/m.

questions.q: At what point in the path of a simple harmonic oscillator is the magnitude of the restoring force at its maximum?
questions.e: Restoring force is directly proportional to displacement (F = -kx). Since displacement is maximum at the extreme positions, the restoring force is also maximum there.
questions.p: Restoring force dey proportional to displacement (F = -kx). Since displacement high reach climax for extreme sides, force sef go maximum for there.

questions.q: A pendulum clock that keeps correct time at sea level is taken to the top of a high mountain. Which of the following describes its behavior?
o: It stops completely due to lower atmospheric pressure
It gains time because g is larger on the mountain
It keeps exact time because mass is constant
It loses time because g is smaller on the mountain
questions.e: Gravity g decreases with altitude. Since T = 2pi × √(L / g), a smaller g results in a larger period T, meaning each oscillation takes longer and the clock loses time.
questions.p: Gravity dey reduce as you go high up mountain. Since T proportional to 1 over square root of g, small g mean big period, so clock go slow down and lose time.

questions.q: Which of the following radiations emitted by a radioactive source is deflected most in a magnetic field directed perpendicularly into the page?
questions.e: Beta-minus particles are high-speed electrons with a very small mass compared to alpha particles and carry a negative charge, while gamma rays and neutrons are uncharged and unaffected by magnetic fields. Due to their small mass-to-charge ratio, beta particles experience maximum deflection.
questions.p: Beta particle na small electron wey get charge and light weight well well, so magnetic field dey bend am pass alpha. Gamma and neutron no get charge at all.

questions.q: The activity of a radioactive nuclide drops from 600 counts per minute to 75 counts per minute in 36 hours. Calculate its half-life.
questions.e: The activity drops through factions: 600 -> 300 (1 half-life) -> 150 (2 half-lives) -> 75 (3 half-lives). Total time = 3 half-lives = 36 hours, so half-life = 36 / 3 = 12 hours.
questions.p: Activity come down from 600 go 300, then 150, then 75. E take 3 half-life reach 75, so if 3 half-life na 36 hours, one half-life na 36 / 3 = 12 hours.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about nuclear fission and nuclear fusion is correct?
o: Fission involves combining light nuclei, whereas fusion involves splitting heavy nuclei
Both fission and fusion decrease the mass number of the participating nuclei
Fission involves splitting a heavy nucleus into lighter nuclei with release of energy
Fusion can easily be controlled at room temperature using magnetic bottles
questions.e: Nuclear fission is the process where a heavy nucleus splits into two or more lighter nuclei, releasing a large amount of energy. Fusion involves joining light nuclei, and both release energy due to mass defect.
questions.p: Nuclear fission na when heavy nucleus break into small small pieces and release energy. Fusion na to join small ones together.

questions.q: A radioactive isotope has a decay constant of 0.0693 per day. Find the time it takes for the number of atoms to reduce to a quarter of its initial value. (Take ln(2) = 0.693)
questions.e: Reducing to a quarter means 2 half-lives have passed. Half-life T_(1/2) = 0.693 / lambda = 0.693 / 0.0693 = 10 days. Total time = 2 × 10 = 20 days.
questions.p: To reduce to quarter mean 2 half-life don pass. Half-life na 0.693 divide by 0.0693, wey be 10 days. Multiply am by 2, you get 20 days.

questions.q: In a radioactive decay process, thorium-234 decays by emitting a beta particle to form protactinium (Pa). What are the mass number and atomic number of the resulting protactinium nucleus respectively?
questions.e: Beta decay increases the atomic number by 1 while the mass number remains unchanged. Thorium has atomic number 90, so Pa will have mass number 234 and atomic number 90 + 1 = 91.
questions.p: When beta particle commot, mass number no dey change, but atomic number go add 1 join. Thorium atomic number na 90, so Pa go get 91, and mass remain 234.

questions.q: If 40 grams of a radioactive material decays to 5 grams in 45 minutes, what is the half-life of the substance?
questions.e: The mass changes as 40 -> 20 (1) -> 10 (2) -> 5 (3 half-lives). Total time = 3 half-lives = 45 minutes, meaning one half-life is 45 / 3 = 15 minutes.
questions.p: Weight change from 40 to 20, then 10, then 5 grams. E take 3 half-life, so 45 minutes divide by 3 na 15 minutes per half-life.

questions.q: What is the primary function of the moderator in a nuclear reactor?
o: To cool down the reactor core and generate high-pressure steam
To absorb excess neutrons to stop the reaction completely
To slow down fast neutrons produced in fission so they can sustain the chain reaction
To shield operators from harmful gamma radiation
questions.e: The moderator (such as graphite or heavy water) slows down fast fission neutrons through elastic collisions so that they have a higher probability of causing further fission of uranium-235.
questions.p: Moderator work na to make fast neutrons slow down small so say dem fit continue the chain reaction with uranium well well.

questions.q: A sample of a radioactive element contains 1.6 x 10²⁰ atoms. If the decay constant is 0.1 per year, how many atoms will have decayed after 10 years? (Take e⁻¹ = 0.368)
questions.e: Remaining atoms N = N_0e^(-lambda × t) = 1.6 x 10²⁰ × e^(-0.1 × 10) = 1.6 x 10²⁰ × 0.368 = 5.888 x 10¹⁹. Decayed atoms = N_0 - N = 1.6 x 10²⁰ - 5.888 x 10¹⁹ = 1.01 x 10²⁰ atoms.
questions.p: First find remaining atoms using exponential formula, wey give about 5.88 x 10¹⁹. Minus am from the original total to find the one wey don spoil, wey come be 1.01 x 10²⁰.

questions.q: If the work function of a metal surface is 3.5 eV, what is the threshold frequency of the incident radiation? (Take Planck's constant h = 6.6 x 10⁻³⁴ J s and 1 eV = 1.6 x 10⁻¹⁹ J)
questions.e: The threshold frequency f_0 is given by W / h, where W is the work function in Joules. Converting 3.5 eV to Joules gives 3.5 x 1.6 x 10⁻¹⁹ J, and dividing by h yields 8.5 x 10¹⁴ Hz.
questions.p: To find threshold frequency, you multiply work function by 1.6 x 10⁻¹⁹ to change am to Joule, then divide am by Planck constant h. Dat give you 8.5 x 10¹⁴ Hz.

questions.q: Which of the following phenomena best demonstrates the particle nature of light?
questions.e: The photoelectric effect can only be explained by treating light as discrete packets of energy called photons, which interact with electrons as particles. Interference, diffraction, and polarisation demonstrate the wave nature of light.
questions.p: Na only photoelectric effect dey show say light get particle nature because e dey carry energy like small small bullet wey we dey call photon. The other ones na wave behavior.

questions.q: Calculate the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons emitted from a metal of work function 2.0 eV when illuminated by light of photon energy 4.5 eV.
questions.e: According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, maximum kinetic energy K_max = E - W. Substituting the values gives 4.5 eV - 2.0 eV = 2.5 eV.
questions.p: Just use Einstein equation, K_max = energy of photon minus work function. E minus W na 4.5 minus 2.0, wey remain 2.5 eV.

questions.q: When the frequency of light incident on a photosensitive metal is doubled, the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons:
o: increases by more than a factor of two
questions.e: From Einstein's equation K_max = hf - W. If frequency f is doubled to 2f, the new kinetic energy is 2hf - W, which is more than double the original (hf - W) because the work function W remains constant.
questions.p: Make you no run enter trap o! E energy depend on hf minus W. If you double frequency, the kinetic energy go increase pass double because the work function na constant.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about photons is correct?
o: Photons possess a rest mass equal to that of an electron
The energy of a photon is inversely proportional to its frequency
Photons carry momentum as well as energy
Photons can be deflected by magnetic fields
questions.e: Photons are massless particles of light that travel at the speed of light in a vacuum, and they carry both energy (E = hf) and momentum (p = h/lambda). They have zero rest mass and carry no charge, so magnetic fields do not deflect them.
questions.p: Photon no get rest mass and magnetic field no dey move am because e no get charge. But e get energy and momentum true true.

questions.q: Light of wavelength 500 nm falls on a metal surface. If the threshold wavelength for the metal is 600 nm, will photoelectrons be emitted?
o: Yes, because the energy of the incident photon is less than the work function
No, because the incident wavelength is less than the threshold wavelength
No, because the incident wavelength is greater than the threshold wavelength
Yes, because the incident wavelength is less than the threshold wavelength
questions.e: Photoemission occurs when the incident wavelength is less than or equal to the threshold wavelength, which corresponds to the incident photon energy being greater than or equal to the work function. Since 500 nm < 600 nm, emission takes place.
questions.p: Since the wavelength wey enter (500 nm) small pass the threshold wavelength (600 nm), e mean say frequency high pass threshold, so electron go commot.

questions.q: In an experiment on the photoelectric effect, stopping potential is plotted against the frequency of incident light. What does the slope of the resulting straight-line graph represent?
o: Ratio of Planck's constant to electronic charge
questions.e: The Einstein equation is e V_s = hf - W, which rearranges to V_s = (h/e)f - W/e. Thus, plotting V_s against f gives a straight line with a slope equal to h/e.
questions.p: From Einstein formula, if you plot V_s against frequency f, the slope na h divide by e (Planck constant over charge of electron).

questions.q: Which of the following physical quantities is a fundamental (base) quantity in the SI system of units?
questions.e: The seven SI base quantities are length, mass, time, electric current, temperature, amount of substance, and luminous intensity. Force, energy and pressure are all derived from these base quantities, but electric current (ampere) is itself a base quantity.
questions.p: SI get seven base quantities: length, mass, time, current, temperature, amount of substance and luminous intensity. Force, energy and pressure na derived ones, but current (ampere) na base quantity straight.

questions.q: The dimension of power (the rate of doing work) in terms of mass [M], length [L] and time [T] is:
questions.e: Work has dimension [M][L]²[T]⁻² and power = work/time, so we divide by [T] to get [M][L]²[T]⁻³. This matches the SI unit watt, which equals joule per second.
questions.p: Work get dimension [M][L]²[T]⁻², and power na work divide by time, so you add one more [T]⁻¹ make e be [M][L]²[T]⁻³. Na so watt (joule per second) dimension be.

questions.q: A block of local 'iroko' wood has a density of 0.65 g/cm³. Express this density in kg/m³.
questions.e: To convert g/cm³ to kg/m³, multiply by 1000, since 1 g/cm³ = 1000 kg/m³. So 0.65 g/cm³ x 1000 = 650 kg/m³.
questions.p: To change g/cm³ to kg/m³, you go multiply by 1000 because 1 g/cm³ = 1000 kg/m³. So 0.65 x 1000 = 650 kg/m³.

questions.q: In fluid mechanics, the terminal velocity v of a small sphere falling through a viscous fluid is given by v = 2r²(rho - sigma)g / (9 x eta), where r is the radius of the sphere, rho and sigma are densities, g is acceleration due to gravity, and eta is the coefficient of viscosity. Using dimensional analysis on this equation, what is the dimension of eta in terms of [M], [L] and [T]?
questions.e: Make eta the subject: eta = 2r²(rho - sigma)g / (9v). The dimensions are r² = [L]², density = [M][L]⁻³, g = [L][T]⁻², and v = [L][T]⁻¹. Multiplying the numerator gives [M][T]⁻² (the L powers cancel: 2 - 3 + 1 = 0), then dividing by v's dimension [L][T]⁻¹ gives [M][L]⁻¹[T]⁻¹, which matches the known unit of viscosity (Pa.s = kg/m/s).
questions.p: Make eta be the subject: eta = 2r²(rho-sigma)g / (9v). r² na [L]², density na [M][L]⁻³, g na [L][T]⁻², v na [L][T]⁻¹. If you multiply the top one, the L powers cancel (2-3+1=0) make e remain [M][T]⁻², then divide by v's [L][T]⁻¹ e go give [M][L]⁻¹[T]⁻¹, wey be the correct viscosity dimension.

questions.q: Which of the following physical quantities is a vector quantity?
questions.e: A vector quantity must have both magnitude and direction. Displacement tells you how far and in which direction an object has moved, unlike distance, speed and energy which are scalars (magnitude only).
questions.p: Vector quantity na quantity wey get both size and direction. Displacement get direction (e dey tell where the body move go), but distance, speed and energy na scalar, dem no get direction.

questions.q: Musa pulls a loaded wheelbarrow using a rope inclined at 30 degrees to the horizontal ground. If the tension in the rope is 40 N, what is the horizontal component of this force (the part that moves the wheelbarrow forward)?
questions.e: The horizontal component of a force F at angle theta to the horizontal is F cos(theta). Here F = 40 N and theta = 30 degrees, so horizontal component = 40 x cos30 = 40 x (√3/2) = 34.64 N.
questions.p: The horizontal component of force na F cos(theta). Here F = 40 N, theta = 30°, so e be 40 x cos30 = 40 x √3/2 = 34.64 N.

questions.q: Two forces of magnitude 10 N and 15 N act at the same point on an object, with an angle of 120 degrees between their directions. Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force.
questions.e: Use the cosine rule for resultant of two forces: R² = P² + Q² + 2PQcos(theta). Here R² = 10² + 15² + 2(10)(15)cos(120) = 100 + 225 - 150 = 175, so R = √175 = 13.23 N.
questions.p: We go use cosine rule: R² = P² + Q² + 2PQcos(theta). So R² = 100 + 225 + 2(10)(15)cos120 = 325 - 150 = 175, R = √175 = 13.23 N.

questions.q: A small object is held in equilibrium on a smooth table by three forces: a force of 9 N acting due east, a force of 12 N acting due north, and a third force F. Calculate the magnitude of F needed to keep the object in equilibrium.
questions.e: Since the 9 N and 12 N forces are at right angles, their resultant is √(9² + 12²) = √(81+144) = √225 = 15 N. For equilibrium, the third force F must be equal in magnitude but opposite in direction to this resultant, so F = 15 N.
questions.p: Since 9 N and 12 N dey form right angle, their resultant na √(9²+12²) = √225 = 15 N. For the body to dey balance (equilibrium), F must equal this resultant for size, just dey face opposite direction, so F = 15 N.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes speed from velocity?
o: Speed is a vector quantity while velocity is a scalar quantity
Both speed and velocity are scalar quantities
Speed is a scalar quantity while velocity is a vector quantity
Both speed and velocity are vector quantities
questions.e: Speed only tells how fast an object moves (magnitude only), so it is a scalar. Velocity includes both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector. This is the standard physics definition.
questions.p: Speed na just how fast something dey move, e no get direction, so na scalar. Velocity get both how fast and the direction, so na vector quantity.

questions.q: An okada (motorcycle) starts from rest and accelerates uniformly, reaching a velocity of 18 m/s after 6 seconds. Calculate the distance it covers during this time.
questions.e: Since motion is uniformly accelerated from rest, average velocity = (u+v)/2 = (0+18)/2 = 9 m/s. Distance = average velocity x time = 9 x 6 = 54 m.
questions.p: Since e start from rest and dey accelerate evenly, average velocity = (0+18)/2 = 9 m/s. Distance = 9 x 6 = 54 m.

questions.q: A driver travels the first half of a journey from Benin to Asaba at a steady speed of 40 km/h and the second half at a steady speed of 60 km/h. What is the average speed for the whole journey?
questions.e: For equal distances at different speeds, average speed = (2 x v1 x v2)/(v1+v2), not the simple average. So average speed = (2 x 40 x 60)/(40+60) = 4800/100 = 48 km/h.
questions.p: Since na equal distance for both parts, you no go just add the two speeds divide by 2. Correct formula na (2 x v1 x v2)/(v1+v2) = (2x40x60)/100 = 48 km/h.

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity of 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s² and ignoring air resistance, find the total time taken for the ball to return to the point where it was thrown.
questions.e: Time to reach the highest point is u/g = 20/10 = 2 s. By symmetry of motion under gravity, the time to fall back equals the time to rise, so total time = 2 x 2 s = 4 s.
questions.p: Time wey e go take reach the highest point na u/g = 20/10 = 2 s. Because the up and down motion dey symmetric, total time wey e go take come back = 2 x 2 = 4 s.

questions.q: At the highest point of the path of a projectile launched at an angle to the horizontal (ignoring air resistance), which statement is TRUE?
o: The horizontal component of velocity is zero
The acceleration of the projectile is zero
The vertical component of velocity is zero
The total velocity of the projectile is zero
questions.e: At the highest point, the projectile stops rising but still moves forward. This means the vertical velocity becomes zero while the horizontal velocity stays the same (since there is no horizontal force). The acceleration due to gravity still acts downward throughout the flight.
questions.p: For the highest point, the thing no dey climb again but e still dey move forward. So the up-down (vertical) speed na zero, but the side-to-side (horizontal) speed still dey there. Gravity still dey pull am down the whole time.

questions.q: An athlete in Kaduna throws a javelin with an initial speed of 24 m/s at an angle of 30° to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s², calculate the maximum height reached by the javelin.
questions.e: Maximum height H = (u sin theta)² / (2g). Here u sin30 = 24 x 0.5 = 12 m/s. So H = 12² / (2 x 10) = 144/20 = 7.2 m.
questions.p: Formula for max height na H = (u sin theta)² / (2g). u sin30 = 24 x 0.5 = 12 m/s. So H = 144/20 = 7.2 m.

questions.q: A small disc in a physics demonstration at a Lagos school rotates uniformly, completing 300 revolutions every minute. What is its angular velocity in rad/s?
questions.e: Angular velocity omega = 2 π N / 60, where N is revolutions per minute. So omega = 2 π x 300 / 60 = 2 π x 5 = 10 π rad/s.
questions.p: Angular speed omega = 2 π N / 60, N na revolutions per minute. So omega = 2 π x 300 / 60 = 2 π x 5 = 10 π rad/s.

questions.q: A car of mass 800 kg goes round a banked curve of radius 50 m at a constant speed of 20 m/s. The curve is banked at an angle such that the car needs no help from friction to stay on the track. Taking g = 10 m/s², calculate tan(theta), where theta is the banking angle.
questions.e: For a car on a frictionless banked curve, tan theta = v² / (r g). Substituting values: tan theta = 20² / (50 x 10) = 400/500 = 0.8. Notice the mass of the car is not needed because it cancels out in the derivation.
questions.p: For banked road wey no need friction, tan theta = v² / (r g). So tan theta = 20² / (50 x 10) = 400/500 = 0.8. The mass of the car no dey affect the answer because e dey cancel for the equation.

questions.q: A boy named Chidi pushes against a classroom wall with a force of 50 N, but the wall does not move. Which statement correctly illustrates Newton's third law of motion in this situation?
o: The wall pushes back on Chidi with a force of 50 N in the opposite direction
The force Chidi applies is converted into heat energy by the wall
The wall exerts no force on Chidi since it is fixed and cannot move
The wall pushes back on Chidi with a smaller force of about 25 N
questions.e: Newton's third law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. Since Chidi pushes the wall with 50 N, the wall pushes back on him with an equal force of 50 N in the opposite direction, even though the wall does not move.
questions.p: Newton third law tell us say action equal reaction but for opposite direction. So if Chidi push wall with 50 N, wall go push am back with 50 N too, even though wall no move.

questions.q: A constant force of 20 N acts on a body of mass 4 kg which is initially at rest, for a time of 0.5 s on a smooth horizontal surface. Calculate the velocity attained by the body at the end of this time.
questions.e: Impulse = Force x time = 20 N x 0.5 s = 10 kg m/s. Since impulse equals change in momentum, 10 = mass x velocity = 4 x v, so v = 10/4 = 2.5 m/s.
questions.p: Impulse be say Force times time: 20 x 0.5 = 10 kg m/s. Since impulse na change in momentum, 10 = 4 x v, so v = 10/4 = 2.5 m/s.

questions.q: A car of mass 800 kg moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest by applying a constant braking force of 2000 N. Calculate the time taken for the car to come to a complete stop.
questions.e: From Newton's second law, deceleration a = F/m = 2000/800 = 2.5 m/s². Using v = u - at with v = 0, u = 20 m/s: 0 = 20 - 2.5t, so t = 20/2.5 = 8 s.
questions.p: From Newton second law, deceleration a = F/m = 2000/800 = 2.5 m/s². Use v = u - at, where v be 0 and u be 20 m/s: 0 = 20 - 2.5t, so t = 20/2.5 = 8 s.

questions.q: A man of mass 60 kg climbs a vertical ladder of height 4 m in 8 seconds. Taking g = 10 m/s², calculate the average power he develops.
questions.e: Work done = mgh = 60 x 10 x 4 = 2400 J. Power = work/time = 2400/8 = 300 W.
questions.p: Work wey e do = mgh = 60 x 10 x 4 = 2400 J. Power = work divide by time = 2400/8 = 300 W.

questions.q: A trailer of mass 1500 kg moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest by a constant braking force acting over a distance of 50 m. Using the work-energy theorem, calculate the magnitude of the braking force.
questions.e: By the work-energy theorem, F x d = (1/2)mv². So F = (0.5 x 1500 x 20²)/50 = 300000/50 = 6000 N.
questions.p: Work-energy theorem say F x d = (1/2)mv². So F = (0.5 x 1500 x 20²)/50 = 300000/50 = 6000 N.

questions.q: A small ball of mass 0.5 kg is released from rest at the top of a smooth frictionless incline of vertical height 1.25 m. Using the principle of conservation of energy, find the speed of the ball when it reaches the bottom of the incline. Take g = 10 m/s².
questions.e: Since the incline is smooth, loss in PE equals gain in KE: mgh = (1/2)mv², so v = √2gh = √(2 x 10 x 1.25) = √25 = 5 m/s.
questions.p: Since the incline no get friction, the PE wey e lose turn to KE: mgh = (1/2)mv², so v = √2gh = √(2 x 10 x 1.25) = √25 = 5 m/s.

questions.q: A pump raises water from a well at a rate of 2 cubic metres per minute to a height of 15 m. If the density of water is 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s², and the pump works at an efficiency of 80%, calculate the power input required to operate the pump.
questions.e: Mass flow rate = 2 x 1000/60 = 33.33 kg/s. Useful output power = mgh per second = 33.33 x 10 x 15 = 5000 W. Since efficiency = output/input, input power = 5000/0.8 = 6250 W.
questions.p: Mass wey dey flow per second = 2 x 1000/60 = 33.33 kg/s. The output power = mgh per second = 33.33 x 10 x 15 = 5000 W. Since efficiency = output/input, input power = 5000/0.8 = 6250 W.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes limiting friction?
o: It is the force that acts only after an object is already in motion
It is the friction that exists only between two lubricated surfaces
It is the maximum value of static friction just before an object begins to slide
It is the force that keeps an object permanently at rest
questions.e: Limiting friction is the greatest value that static friction can reach before the object starts to move. Once this value is exceeded, the object slides and kinetic friction takes over.
questions.p: Limiting friction na the highest level wey static friction fit reach before the object go start to move. Once e pass that level, the object go begin slide and na kinetic friction go dey act.

questions.q: A technician uses a crowbar as a lever to lift a block of stone weighing 450 N from the ground. The fulcrum is positioned such that the load arm is 0.3 m and the effort arm is 1.2 m. Assuming the lever works as a perfect (frictionless) machine, calculate the minimum effort needed to just lift the stone.
questions.e: For a lever, effort x effort arm = load x load arm. So effort = (450 x 0.3)/1.2 = 112.5 N. This is the minimum force needed since the machine is assumed frictionless.
questions.p: For lever, effort times effort arm go equal load times load arm. So effort be (450 x 0.3)/1.2 = 112.5 N. Na the smallest force wey go fit lift the stone since no friction dey.

questions.q: A wooden block of mass 5 kg rests on a horizontal laboratory bench. A horizontal pulling force of 20 N is just enough to make the block start sliding. Taking g = 10 m/s², calculate the coefficient of static friction between the block and the bench surface.
questions.e: At the point of just moving, the applied force equals the limiting frictional force, F = mu x m x g. So mu = F/(mg) = 20/(5 x 10) = 0.4.
questions.p: Just as the block dey about to move, the force wey dem apply go equal the limiting friction, F = mu x m x g. So mu = 20/(5 x 10) = 0.4.

questions.q: A block-and-tackle pulley system at a construction site in Minna has a velocity ratio of 6. A worker, Musa, applies an effort of 100 N to raise a load of 480 N. Calculate the percentage efficiency of the pulley system.
questions.e: Mechanical advantage = load/effort = 480/100 = 4.8. Efficiency = (MA/VR) x 100 = (4.8/6) x 100 = 80%. This shows the system loses some energy to friction since efficiency is below 100%.
questions.p: Mechanical advantage = load/effort = 480/100 = 4.8. Efficiency = (MA/VR) x 100 = (4.8/6) x 100 = 80%. Since e no reach 100%, e mean say some energy dey waste as friction.

questions.q: Which of the following best states Hooke's law for an elastic material?
o: The extension produced in a material is inversely proportional to the applied force at all times
The extension produced in a material increases without limit as the applied force increases
The extension produced in a material is directly proportional to the applied force, provided the elastic limit is not exceeded
The stress in a material is always equal to its strain regardless of the force applied
questions.e: Hooke's law says that within the elastic limit, extension (or compression) is directly proportional to the applied force. Beyond the elastic limit, this proportionality breaks down and the material may deform permanently.
questions.p: Hooke's law talk say as long as the material never pass its elastic limit, the extension go dey proportional to the force wey dem apply. If e pass the limit, the proportion no go hold again.

questions.q: A spring stretches by 8.0 cm when a force of 40 N is applied to it, without exceeding its elastic limit. Calculate the force constant (spring constant) of the spring.
questions.e: Force constant k = F/x. First convert 8.0 cm to metres: 8.0 cm = 0.08 m. So k = 40 N / 0.08 m = 500 N/m.
questions.p: k = F/x. Convert 8.0 cm to metre: 0.08 m. So k = 40/0.08 = 500 N/m.

questions.q: Two identical springs, Chidi's spring A and Chidi's spring B, each have a force constant of 250 N/m. They are joined side by side (in parallel) and used to support a single load, so that both springs stretch by the same amount. Calculate the effective force constant of the combination.
questions.e: For springs in parallel, the effective force constant is the sum of the individual constants: k_eff = k1 + k2 = 250 + 250 = 500 N/m. This is because both springs share the load and stretch equally, so their stiffnesses add up.
questions.p: For springs wey dey side by side (parallel), the total k na the sum of the two: 250 + 250 = 500 N/m. The two springs dey carry the load together so their stiffness just add up.

questions.q: A metal wire of length 2.0 m and cross-sectional area 1.0 mm² stretches by 1.0 mm when a force of 100 N is applied, without exceeding its elastic limit. Calculate the Young's modulus of the wire material.
questions.e: Young's modulus E = (F x L) / (A x e). Convert units: A = 1.0 mm² = 1.0 x 10⁻⁶ m², e = 1.0 mm = 1.0 x 10⁻³ m. So E = (100 x 2.0) / (1.0 x 10⁻⁶ x 1.0 x 10⁻³) = 200 / (1.0 x 10⁻⁹) = 2.0 x 10¹¹ N/m².
questions.p: E = (F x L)/(A x e). Convert area to 1.0 x 10⁻⁶ m² and extension to 1.0 x 10⁻³ m. E = (100 x 2.0)/(1.0x10⁻⁶ x 1.0x10⁻³) = 200/1.0x10⁻⁹ = 2.0 x 10¹¹ N/m².

questions.q: A nurse at a clinic in Enugu presses the tip of a hypodermic needle against a patient's skin. The tip has a cross-sectional area of 0.0005 cm², and the nurse applies a force of 2.5 N. Calculate the pressure exerted by the needle tip on the skin.
questions.e: First convert area to m²: 0.0005 cm² = 0.0005 x 10⁻⁴ m² = 5 x 10⁻⁸ m². Pressure = Force / Area = 2.5 / (5 x 10⁻⁸) = 5 x 10⁷ N/m². The tiny area of the sharp needle tip makes the pressure very large even though the force is small.
questions.p: Make we change the area go m² first: 0.0005 cm² = 5 x 10⁻⁸ m². Pressure = Force / Area = 2.5 / (5 x 10⁻⁸) = 5 x 10⁷ N/m². Na why sharp needle fit press hard enter skin even though the force small.

questions.q: A barometer tube contains a column of mercury 76 cm high. Calculate the pressure exerted by this column of mercury. (Density of mercury = 13600 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²)
questions.e: Pressure in a liquid column is given by P = h x density x g. First change 76 cm to 0.76 m, then P = 0.76 x 13600 x 10 = 103360 N/m², which is about 1.034 x 10⁵ N/m². This is the usual value of atmospheric pressure measured by a mercury barometer.
questions.p: Pressure for liquid column be P = h x density x g. Change 76 cm go 0.76 m, then P = 0.76 x 13600 x 10 = 103360 N/m², wey be around 1.034 x 10⁵ N/m². Na dis kain value dem dey get for mercury barometer wey dey show atmospheric pressure.

questions.q: A metal block of mass 450 g and volume 60 cm³ is suspended from a spring balance and lowered until it is completely submerged in a liquid of density 800 kg/m³. Calculate the new reading on the spring balance. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.e: Weight in air = mg = 0.45 x 10 = 4.5 N. Upthrust = density of liquid x volume x g = 800 x (60 x 10⁻⁶) x 10 = 0.48 N. Apparent weight = weight in air minus upthrust = 4.5 - 0.48 = 4.02 N, which is what the spring balance reads.
questions.p: Weight for air = mg = 0.45 x 10 = 4.5 N. Upthrust = density of liquid x volume x g = 800 x (60 x 10⁻⁶) x 10 = 0.48 N. Apparent weight = 4.5 - 0.48 = 4.02 N, na im spring balance go show.

questions.q: A cube of wax floats in water with one-fifth of its volume above the surface. If the same cube is placed in a sample of groundnut oil of density 880 kg/m³, what fraction of its volume will now float above the oil's surface? (Density of water = 1000 kg/m³)
questions.e: In water, 4/5 of the wax is submerged, so density of wax = (4/5) x 1000 = 800 kg/m³. In oil, the submerged fraction equals density of wax divided by density of oil = 800/880 = 10/11, so the fraction above the oil surface is 1 - 10/11 = 1/11.
questions.p: For water, 4/5 of the wax dey inside, so density of wax = (4/5) x 1000 = 800 kg/m³. For oil, the part wey dey inside na density of wax divide by density of oil = 800/880 = 10/11, so the part wey dey outside na 1 - 10/11 = 1/11.

questions.q: What is the value of absolute zero (the lowest temperature theoretically attainable) on the Celsius scale?
questions.e: Absolute zero is the temperature at which particles have minimum kinetic energy. On the Celsius scale this corresponds to -273 °C (0 K). This is a fixed, well-known physical constant.
questions.p: Absolute zero na di temperature wey particles get di least energy wey dem fit get. For Celsius scale, e dey equal -273 °C (wey be 0 K).

questions.q: A brass rod of length 2.0 m at 20 °C is heated until its temperature becomes 100 °C. If the coefficient of linear expansion of brass is 1.9 x 10⁻⁵ per °C, calculate the increase in length of the rod.
questions.e: Increase in length = L x alpha x change in temperature = 2.0 x 1.9x10⁻⁵ x (100-20) = 2.0 x 1.9x10⁻⁵ x 80 = 3.04 x 10⁻³ m. Only option A matches this correct substitution.
questions.p: Di extra length = L x alpha x change for temperature = 2.0 x 1.9x10⁻⁵ x 80 = 3.04 x 10⁻³ m. Na option A be di correct answer wey match dis calculation.

questions.q: A square copper plate has sides of length 50 cm at 0 °C. If the coefficient of linear expansion of copper is 2.0 x 10⁻⁵ per °C, calculate the increase in the area of the plate when it is heated to 100 °C.
questions.e: The coefficient of area (superficial) expansion is 2 x alpha = 4.0 x 10⁻⁵ per °C. Increase in area = A0 x 2alpha x change in temperature = (0.5 x 0.5) x 4.0x10⁻⁵ x 100 = 0.25 x 4.0x10⁻³ = 1.0 x 10⁻³ m². Candidates who forget to double alpha for area expansion will pick a wrong option.
questions.p: Di area expansion coefficient na 2 x alpha = 4.0 x 10⁻⁵ per °C. Increase for area = A0 x 2alpha x change for temperature = 0.25 x 4.0x10⁻³ = 1.0 x 10⁻³ m². If you forget to double di alpha for area, you go miss di answer.

questions.q: A bimetallic strip is made by joining a strip of brass to a strip of iron of the same length, with brass having a larger coefficient of linear expansion than iron. When the straight strip is heated uniformly, in which direction does it bend, and why?
o: It bends towards the iron side, because brass expands more than iron and forms the outer (longer) curve
It bends towards the brass side, because iron expands more than brass
It remains perfectly straight, because both metals expand by the same amount
It bends towards the brass side, because brass contracts while iron expands
questions.e: Since brass has a higher coefficient of linear expansion, it lengthens more than iron for the same temperature rise. This forces the strip to curve, with brass on the outside of the bend, so the strip bends towards the iron (shorter) side.
questions.p: Since brass get bigger expansion coefficient pass iron, e go stretch pass iron when dem heat dem together. Dis one go make di strip curve, make brass dey outside, so di strip go bend go iron side.

questions.q: A technician in a workshop in Kano compresses 600 cm³ of air in a syringe at a constant temperature until its pressure rises from 100 kPa to a new value, reducing the volume to 300 cm³. Using Boyle's law, calculate the new pressure of the air.
questions.e: Boyle's law: P1V1 = P2V2 at constant temperature. So P2 = (100 kPa x 600 cm³) / 300 cm³ = 200 kPa.
questions.p: Boyle law talk say P1V1 equal P2V2 if temperature no change. So P2 = (100 x 600)/300 = 200 kPa.

questions.q: A balloon seller in Lagos has a balloon containing 2.0 litres of gas at a pressure of 1.0 atm and a temperature of 300 K. The balloon is heated and compressed so that the pressure becomes 2.0 atm and the temperature rises to 450 K. Using the combined gas law, calculate the new volume of the gas.
questions.p: Combined gas law say P1V1/T1 equal P2V2/T2. V2 = 2.0 x (1.0/2.0) x (450/300) = 1.5 litres.

questions.q: A steel cylinder contains 8.0 g of oxygen gas (molar mass = 32 g/mol) at a pressure of 2.0 x 10⁵ Pa and a temperature of 300 K. Using the ideal gas equation PV = nRT, with R = 8.314 J/(mol K), calculate the volume occupied by the gas.
questions.e: Number of moles n = mass/molar mass = 8.0/32 = 0.25 mol. From PV = nRT, V = nRT/P = (0.25 x 8.314 x 300) / (2.0 x 10⁵) = 623.55 / 200000 = 3.12 x 10⁻³ m³.

questions.q: A fixed mass of an ideal gas has its volume increased from V to 3V while its pressure is reduced from P to P/2. Using the combined gas law, find the ratio of the final absolute temperature to the initial absolute temperature of the gas.
questions.e: From P1V1/T1 = P2V2/T2, the ratio T2/T1 = (P2V2)/(P1V1) = ((P/2)(3V))/(PV) = 3/2 = 1.5. So the final temperature is 1.5 times the initial temperature.
questions.p: From P1V1/T1 = P2V2/T2, T2/T1 = ((P/2)(3V))/(PV) = 3/2 = 1.5. So the final temperature na 1.5 times the first one.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines the specific heat capacity of a substance?
o: The quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of a unit mass of the substance by one degree without a change of state.
The quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of the substance to its boiling point.
The quantity of heat released when the substance changes from liquid to solid.
The quantity of heat required to melt a unit mass of the substance without a change in temperature.
questions.e: Specific heat capacity is defined as the heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 K (or 1°C), with no change of state occurring. Options about melting or boiling describe latent heat, not specific heat capacity.
questions.p: Specific heat capacity na the heat wey you need to raise temperature of 1 kg of substance by 1 degree, no change of state dey happen. The other options dey talk about melting or boiling wey be latent heat matter, no be specific heat capacity.

questions.q: A metal sample of mass 0.4 kg is heated from 20°C to 100°C by supplying 14,400 J of heat energy, with no change of state occurring. Calculate the specific heat capacity of the metal in J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.

A sample of water of mass 0.25 kg at 100°C absorbs 5.65 x 10⁵ J of heat energy and is completely converted to steam at 100°C, with no change in temperature. Calculate the specific latent heat of vaporization of the water, in J kg⁻¹.
questions.e: For a change of state at constant temperature, Q = mL, so L = Q/m. L = 5.65 x 10⁵ / 0.25 = 2.26 x 10⁶ J/kg.
questions.p: For change of state wey temperature no dey change, Q = mL, so L = Q/m. L = 5.65 x 10⁵ / 0.25 = 2.26 x 10⁶ J/kg.

questions.q: A 0.5 kg block of ice at 0°C is dropped into 1.5 kg of water at 30°C inside a well-insulated flask, so that no heat is lost to the surroundings. Given that the specific latent heat of fusion of ice is 3.36 x 10⁵ J kg⁻¹ and the specific heat capacity of water is 4200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine the final steady temperature of the mixture after all the ice has melted.
questions.e: Heat lost by the warm water equals heat used to melt the ice plus heat used to warm the melted ice to the final temperature T. Setting up: 1.5(4200)(30-T) = 0.5(336000) + 0.5(4200)T. This gives 189000 - 6300T = 168000 + 2100T, so 21000 = 8400T, and T = 2.5°C.
questions.p: Heat wey the warm water lose go equal the heat wey melt the ice plus the heat wey warm the melted ice reach final temperature T. If you set am up: 1.5(4200)(30-T) = 0.5(336000) + 0.5(4200)T, e go give 189000 - 6300T = 168000 + 2100T, so 21000 = 8400T, meaning T = 2.5°C.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains how heat travels through a metal spoon when one end is placed inside a hot pot of soup?
o: Heat energy is passed from particle to particle through vibration and free-electron movement, without the particles changing position permanently
Heat energy evaporates from the hot end and condenses at the cold end
Heat energy is carried by moving fluid particles from the hot end to the cold end
Heat energy is transferred by electromagnetic waves travelling through the metal
questions.e: In solids like metals, heat moves by conduction. The particles vibrate more as they get hot and pass this energy to neighbouring particles, and free electrons also help carry the energy along. The particles themselves do not move from one end to the other.
questions.p: For metal like spoon, heat dey waka through conduction. The particles go just vibrate well-well and pass the energy go their neighbour, plus free electrons wey dey help carry am. The particles no dey waka from one end go the other end.

questions.q: A metal bar of length 0.50 m and uniform cross-sectional area 2.0 x 10⁻⁴ m² has its two ends kept steadily at 100 degrees C and 20 degrees C. If the thermal conductivity of the metal is 400 W/m per degree C, calculate the rate of heat flow through the bar.
questions.e: Using Q/t = kA(delta T)/L, we have k = 400, A = 2.0x10⁻⁴, delta T = 100 - 20 = 80, L = 0.50. So Q/t = 400 x 2.0x10⁻⁴ x 80 / 0.50 = 12.8 W.
questions.p: We use the formula Q/t = kA(delta T)/L. k = 400, A = 2.0x10⁻⁴, delta T = 80, L = 0.50. If you calculate am well, you go see say Q/t = 12.8 W.

questions.q: When water in an open pot is heated steadily from below, convection currents are set up in the liquid. Which of the following correctly describes what happens to the heated water and why?
o: Heated water sinks to the bottom because it becomes denser than the surrounding water
Heated water stays at the bottom because convection only occurs in gases, not liquids
Heated water rises to the top because it becomes less dense than the surrounding cooler water
Heated water moves only sideways because of surface tension, without rising or sinking
questions.e: When water at the bottom is heated, it expands and becomes less dense than the cooler water above it. The less dense warm water rises while the cooler, denser water sinks to take its place, setting up a convection current.
questions.p: When the water for down dey heat, e go expand and e density go reduce pass the cold water wey dey up. So the warm water go rise go up, the cold one go come down, and that one go start convection current.

questions.q: A blacksmith's furnace in Kano radiates heat uniformly in all directions like a point source. A worker standing 2 m from the furnace feels a certain intensity of radiant heat. If the worker moves back to a new position 4 m from the furnace, by what factor does the intensity of the radiant heat received change?
o: It reduces to 1/2 of the original intensity
It reduces to 1/4 of the original intensity
It reduces to 1/16 of the original intensity
It reduces to 1/8 of the original intensity
questions.e: Radiant heat intensity from a point source follows the inverse square law: intensity is proportional to 1/r². Doubling the distance from 2 m to 4 m means the intensity changes by a factor of (2/4)² = 1/4. So the worker now receives only one quarter of the original intensity.
questions.p: Radiant heat from one point source dey follow inverse square law: intensity dey proportional to 1/r². If distance double from 2 m go 4 m, the factor na (2/4)² = 1/4. So na quarter of the original heat the worker go feel now.

questions.q: A vibrating tuning fork produces a wave that completes one full oscillation every 0.02 seconds. What is the frequency of the wave?
questions.e: Frequency is the reciprocal of period, f = 1/T. Here T = 0.02 s, so f = 1/0.02 = 50 Hz.
questions.p: Frequency na 1 divide by period, f = 1/T. T be 0.02 s, so f = 1/0.02 = 50 Hz.

questions.q: A water wave in a ripple tank has a frequency of 25 Hz and a wavelength of 2 m. Calculate the speed of the wave.
questions.e: Wave speed is found using v = f x wavelength. So v = 25 Hz x 2 m = 50 m/s.
questions.p: To find wave speed, use v = f x wavelength. So v = 25 Hz x 2 m = 50 m/s.

questions.q: Market women in Onitsha can hear a vendor's voice across a busy, dusty stall, but radio signals from a nearby FM station can reach the moon (in principle) without any air at all. Which statement correctly explains this difference?
o: Sound waves travel faster than radio waves in air
Sound waves are mechanical and need a material medium, while radio waves are electromagnetic and can travel through vacuum
Radio waves are mechanical waves that need air to travel
Sound waves can travel through a vacuum just like radio waves
questions.e: Sound is a mechanical wave, so it needs particles of a medium (like air) to vibrate and transfer energy. Radio waves are electromagnetic waves, which do not need any medium and can travel through empty space.
questions.p: Sound na mechanical wave, e need particles for medium (like air) before e fit waka. Radio wave na electromagnetic wave, e no need medium at all, e fit pass through empty space.

questions.q: A sound wave of frequency 500 Hz travels in air at a speed of 340 m/s. It then enters water, where its speed increases to 1500 m/s. Since the frequency of a wave does not change when it moves from one medium to another, what is the wavelength of the sound wave inside the water?
questions.e: Frequency stays the same across the boundary, only speed and wavelength change. Using v = f x wavelength, wavelength = v/f = 1500/500 = 3 m.
questions.p: Frequency no dey change when wave cross from one medium go another, na speed and wavelength go change. Use v = f x wavelength, so wavelength = 1500/500 = 3 m.

questions.q: For a listener to hear a distinct echo (that is, a reflected sound heard separately from the original sound), the human ear needs the reflected sound to arrive at least 0.1 s after the direct sound. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, what is the minimum distance between the listener and the reflecting wall for a distinct echo to be heard?
questions.e: The sound travels to the wall and back in 0.1 s, so distance = speed x time / 2 = 340 x 0.1 / 2 = 17 m. This is the shortest gap between listener and wall that still gives a separate echo.
questions.p: The sound go waka reach wall and come back for 0.1 s, so distance be speed x time divide by 2 = 340 x 0.1 / 2 = 17 m. Na the shortest gap wey go still make you hear clear echo.

questions.q: A closed pipe (closed at one end, open at the other) has a length of 42.5 cm. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, calculate the fundamental frequency produced by this pipe.
questions.e: For a closed pipe, the fundamental wavelength is 4 times the length, so wavelength = 4 x 0.425 m = 1.7 m. Frequency = speed / wavelength = 340 / 1.7 = 200 Hz.
questions.p: For closed pipe, the first wavelength na 4 times the length, so wavelength = 4 x 0.425 = 1.7 m. Frequency = speed / wavelength = 340 / 1.7 = 200 Hz.

questions.q: In a resonance tube experiment with a vibrating tuning fork, the first position of resonance (shortest air column) is found at 12 cm and the next position of resonance is found at 46 cm, measured from the open end of the tube. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, what is the frequency of the tuning fork?
questions.e: The distance between two successive resonance positions equals half a wavelength, so half-wavelength = 46 - 12 = 34 cm, giving wavelength = 68 cm = 0.68 m. Frequency = speed / wavelength = 340 / 0.68 = 500 Hz.
questions.p: The gap between the two resonance points na half wavelength, so half-wavelength = 46 - 12 = 34 cm, wavelength = 68 cm = 0.68 m. Frequency = speed / wavelength = 340 / 0.68 = 500 Hz.

questions.q: Ngozi stands somewhere between two tall cliffs that are 850 m apart, in a straight line with both cliffs. She claps once and hears the first echo after 2 seconds and the second echo (from the other cliff) after 3 seconds. Taking the speed of sound as 340 m/s, how far is Ngozi from the nearer cliff?
questions.e: Distance to nearer cliff = speed x time / 2 = 340 x 2 / 2 = 340 m, since sound travels there and back in 2 s. Checking: distance to farther cliff = 340 x 3 / 2 = 510 m, and 340 + 510 = 850 m, which matches the given gap between the cliffs, confirming the answer.
questions.p: Distance to the near cliff = speed x time / 2 = 340 x 2 / 2 = 340 m, because sound waka go and come back for 2 s. If you check, distance to the far cliff = 340 x 3 / 2 = 510 m, and 340 + 510 = 850 m wey match the gap wey dem give, so e correct.

questions.q: A ray of light is sent so that it travels exactly along the normal to a plane mirror, striking the mirror perpendicularly. What is the angle of reflection?
questions.e: The normal is the line perpendicular to the mirror surface. If the incident ray lies along the normal, the angle between the incident ray and the normal is 0°. By the law of reflection, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, so it is also 0°.
questions.p: Normal na di line wey dey perpendicular to di mirror. If di ray dey waka along dis normal, e mean say di angle wey e make with di normal na 0°. Since angle of reflection go equal angle of incidence, e go also be 0°.

questions.q: A concave mirror has a focal length of 15 cm. An object is placed 10 cm in front of the mirror. What is the magnitude of the image distance formed?
questions.e: Using the mirror formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, with f = 15 cm and u = 10 cm: 1/v = 1/15 - 1/10 = -1/30, so v = -30 cm. The negative sign shows the image is virtual (behind the mirror), and its magnitude is 30 cm.
questions.p: Using mirror formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, with f = 15 cm, u = 10 cm: 1/v = 1/15 - 1/10 = -1/30, so v = -30 cm. Di negative sign show say na virtual image (e dey behind di mirror), and di size na 30 cm.

questions.q: Chidinma is 1.6 m tall and stands upright in front of a large vertical plane mirror fixed on a wall. What is the minimum length of the mirror needed so that she can see her full image, from head to toe, no matter how far she stands from the mirror?
questions.e: For a plane mirror, the minimum mirror length needed to see a full-length image of a person is exactly half the person's height, regardless of the distance from the mirror. So the minimum length = 1.6 m / 2 = 0.8 m.
questions.p: For plane mirror, di minimum length wey you need to see your full body inside am na half of your height, no matter how far you stand from di mirror. So minimum length = 1.6 m / 2 = 0.8 m.

questions.q: A convex mirror has a radius of curvature of 24 cm. An object is placed 18 cm in front of the mirror. Using the sign convention where real object and image distances are positive and the focal length of a convex mirror is negative, calculate the magnitude of the image distance.
questions.e: Focal length f = -R/2 = -24/2 = -12 cm. Using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u: -1/12 = 1/v + 1/18, so 1/v = -1/12 - 1/18 = -5/36, giving v = -7.2 cm. The magnitude of the image distance is 7.2 cm.
questions.p: Focal length f = -R/2 = -24/2 = -12 cm. Using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u: -1/12 = 1/v + 1/18, so 1/v = -1/12 - 1/18 = -5/36, e give v = -7.2 cm. Di size of di image distance na 7.2 cm.

questions.q: A ray of light passes from a less dense medium into a denser medium, bending towards the normal. Which of the following correctly defines the refractive index, n, of the denser medium with respect to the less dense medium?
o: n = sine of angle of incidence / sine of angle of refraction
n = sine of angle of refraction / sine of angle of incidence
n = speed of light in denser medium / speed of light in less dense medium
n = angle of incidence / angle of refraction
questions.e: Refractive index from a rarer to a denser medium is defined as the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence (in the rarer medium) to the sine of the angle of refraction (in the denser medium). This is Snell's law, n = sin i / sin r. Using angles directly (not their sines) or speeds the wrong way round gives incorrect definitions.
questions.p: Refractive index na sine of angle of incidence divide by sine of angle of refraction, dat one na Snell's law. If you use di angle demsef (no sine) or you flip di speed ratio, e go wrong.

questions.q: A beam of light travels from air into a transparent liquid of refractive index 1.6. The angle of incidence in air is 53° (take sin 53° = 0.80). Calculate the angle of refraction in the liquid, to the nearest whole degree.
questions.e: By Snell's law, n = sin i / sin r, so sin r = sin i / n = 0.80 / 1.6 = 0.5. Taking the inverse sine of 0.5 gives r = 30°. The light bends towards the normal because it enters a denser medium, so the refraction angle must be smaller than 53°.
questions.p: Snell's law talk say sin r = sin i / n = 0.80/1.6 = 0.5, so r = arcsin(0.5) = 30°. Since di light dey enter denser medium, di angle must reduce pass 53°, and 30° fit am well.

questions.q: A diver under a swimming pool shines a torchlight upward towards the water surface. The refractive index of water with respect to air is 4/3. Calculate the critical angle for the water-air boundary, to the nearest 0.1°.
questions.e: At the critical angle, light travels along the surface, meaning the angle of refraction is 90°. Since n(water to air) = 1/n(water) relative to air = 1/(4/3) = 3/4, we use sin C = 1/n = 3/4 = 0.75, giving C = arcsin(0.75) = 48.6°. Beyond this angle, total internal reflection occurs instead of the light escaping into the air.
questions.p: Critical angle na di angle wey di refracted ray go dey waka follow di surface (90°). Since water get refractive index 4/3 relative to air, sin C = 1/(4/3) = 0.75, so C = arcsin(0.75) = 48.6°. Pass dat angle, na total internal reflection go happen.

questions.q: An object of height 2 cm is placed 15 cm in front of a converging (convex) lens of focal length 10 cm. Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u (with u, v and f all taken as positive for a real object and real image), calculate the height of the image formed.
questions.e: From 1/f = 1/v + 1/u: 1/10 = 1/v + 1/15, so 1/v = 1/10 - 1/15 = 1/30, giving v = 30 cm. Magnification m = v/u = 30/15 = 2. Image height = m x object height = 2 x 2 cm = 4 cm.
questions.p: From 1/f = 1/v + 1/u: 1/10 = 1/v + 1/15, so 1/v = 1/30, dat mean v = 30 cm. Magnification m = v/u = 30/15 = 2, so image height = 2 x 2 cm = 4 cm.

questions.q: A parallel-plate capacitor is charged by a battery and then disconnected so that the charge on it stays constant. If the plate separation is then doubled (with the charge unchanged), what happens to the potential difference across the plates?
questions.e: Capacitance C = epsilon0 A/d, so doubling d halves C. Since charge Q is fixed and V = Q/C, halving C makes V double. This shows V and d are directly related when Q is constant.
questions.p: C = epsilon0 A/d, so if d double, C go reduce to half. Since Q no change, V = Q/C, so when C reduce to half, V go double.

questions.q: Three capacitors of capacitance 4 microfarad, 5 microfarad and 6 microfarad are connected in parallel across a battery. Calculate the equivalent capacitance of the combination.
questions.e: For capacitors in parallel, the equivalent capacitance is the sum of the individual capacitances: C = 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 microfarad. Parallel connection simply adds up capacitance values, unlike series connection.
questions.p: For parallel capacitors, you just add dem together: 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 microfarad. Na simple addition, no reciprocal wahala like series own.

questions.q: Two point charges of +2 x 10⁻⁶ C and +3 x 10⁻⁶ C are placed 0.3 m apart in air. Using k = 9 x 10⁹ N m²/C², calculate the electrostatic force between them.
questions.e: By Coulomb's law, F = k q1 q2 / r² = (9x10⁹ x 2x10⁻⁶ x 3x10⁻⁶) / (0.3)² = (9x10⁹ x 6x10⁻¹²) / 0.09 = 0.054/0.09 = 0.6 N. Remember to square the distance, not just use it directly.
questions.p: Coulomb law: F = k q1 q2 / r² = (9x10⁹ x 2x10⁻⁶ x 3x10⁻⁶) / (0.3)² = 0.054/0.09 = 0.6 N. Make sure you square the distance, no just use am as e be.

questions.q: A parallel-plate capacitor of capacitance 8 microfarad is charged to a potential difference of 200 V and then disconnected from the battery, so its charge stays fixed. A dielectric slab of dielectric constant 4 is now inserted completely between the plates. Calculate the new potential difference across the capacitor.
questions.e: When the dielectric slab is inserted, the new capacitance becomes C' = 4 x 8 = 32 microfarad, but the charge Q stays the same because the battery is disconnected. Using V = Q/C, since C increases 4 times, V decreases 4 times: V' = 200/4 = 50 V. Many students wrongly multiply instead of dividing since C increased.
questions.p: Once dielectric enter, capacitance go increase to 4 x 8 = 32 microfarad, but charge Q no change because battery don disconnect. V = Q/C, so if C increase 4 times, V go reduce 4 times: V' = 200/4 = 50 V. No dey multiply am, na divide because C don increase.

questions.q: In a laboratory experiment, Ngozi connects a resistor of 15 ohms to a battery so that a steady current of 0.8 A flows through it. Using Ohm's law, calculate the voltage across the resistor.
questions.e: Ohm's law states V = IR. So V = 15 ohms x 0.8 A = 12 V. The other options come from wrong operations like dividing or adding instead of multiplying.
questions.p: Ohm's law talk say V = IR. So V = 15 x 0.8 = 12 V. The other answers na from wrong maths like dividing or adding instead of multiply.

questions.q: An 8-ohm resistor and a 12-ohm resistor are connected in parallel. This parallel combination is then connected in series with a 5-ohm resistor across a battery. Calculate the total resistance of the circuit.
questions.e: For resistors in parallel, 1/Rp = 1/8 + 1/12, giving Rp = (8x12)/(8+12) = 96/20 = 4.8 ohms. Adding the series resistor: Total R = 4.8 + 5 = 9.8 ohms. The wrong options either forget to add the series resistor or wrongly add all values directly.
questions.p: For parallel resistors, Rp = (8x12)/(8+12) = 96/20 = 4.8 ohms. Then add the series 5 ohms: Total = 4.8 + 5 = 9.8 ohms. The wrong options no add the series resistor well or just add everything anyhow.

questions.q: A dry cell with e.m.f. 3.0 V and internal resistance 0.4 ohms is connected to an external resistor of 2.6 ohms. Calculate the current flowing in the circuit.
questions.e: The current in a circuit with e.m.f. and internal resistance is I = E/(R + r) = 3.0/(2.6 + 0.4) = 3.0/3.0 = 1.0 A. Ignoring internal resistance (3.0/2.6) or using only internal resistance (3.0/0.4) gives the wrong distractors.
questions.p: Current be I = E/(R+r) = 3.0/(2.6+0.4) = 3.0/3.0 = 1.0 A. If person forget internal resistance e go get 3.0/2.6, or if e use only internal resistance e go get 3.0/0.4 - both na wrong answer.

questions.q: A fluorescent lamp in a classroom is rated 40 W. If it is left switched on for 6 hours a day, calculate the electrical energy it consumes in one day, in kilowatt-hours (kWh).
questions.e: Energy (kWh) = Power (kW) x Time (h). Power = 40 W = 0.04 kW, so Energy = 0.04 x 6 = 0.24 kWh.
questions.p: Energy for kWh = Power (for kW) multiply Time (for hour). 40 W na 0.04 kW, so 0.04 x 6 give 0.24 kWh.

questions.q: In Mama Chidi's shop, a 1000 W pressing iron is used for 30 minutes, a 1500 W water heater is used for 20 minutes, and a 60 W bulb is used for 5 hours. If electricity costs ₦60 per kWh, calculate the total cost of running these three appliances.
questions.e: Convert each appliance's usage to kWh: iron = 1000 W x 0.5 h = 500 Wh; heater = 1500 W x (20/60) h = 500 Wh; bulb = 60 W x 5 h = 300 Wh. Total = 1300 Wh = 1.3 kWh. Cost = 1.3 x ₦60 = ₦78.00.
questions.p: Change each appliance time go hour: iron = 1000 W x 0.5 h = 500 Wh, heater = 1500 W x (20/60) h = 500 Wh, bulb = 60 W x 5 h = 300 Wh. Total na 1300 Wh wey be 1.3 kWh. Cost = 1.3 x ₦60 = ₦78.00.

questions.q: A resistor of fixed resistance R is connected across a voltage source and dissipates power P. If the voltage across the resistor is doubled while R stays the same, by what factor does the power dissipated increase?
questions.e: Power is given by P = V²/R. If V doubles, V² becomes 4 times as large, so the new power is 4 times the original power, since R does not change.
questions.p: Power na P = V²/R. If V double, V² go be 4 times wetin e be before, so power go also increase by 4 times since R no change.

questions.q: A trader compares an old incandescent bulb rated 100 W with a new LED bulb rated 20 W, both giving the same brightness. Each bulb is used for 8 hours daily for 30 days, and electricity costs ₦50 per kWh. Calculate how much money the trader saves in those 30 days by using the LED bulb instead of the incandescent bulb.
questions.e: Incandescent energy = 100 W x 8 h x 30 = 24000 Wh = 24 kWh, costing 24 x ₦50 = ₦1200. LED energy = 20 W x 8 h x 30 = 4800 Wh = 4.8 kWh, costing 4.8 x ₦50 = ₦240. Savings = ₦1200 - ₦240 = ₦960.
questions.p: Incandescent energy = 100 W x 8 h x 30 = 24 kWh, e go cost 24 x ₦50 = ₦1200. LED energy = 20 W x 8 h x 30 = 4.8 kWh, e go cost 4.8 x ₦50 = ₦240. Wetin dem save = ₦1200 - ₦240 = ₦960.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the magnetic field lines of a bar magnet?
o: They terminate at the centre of the magnet where the field is strongest
They form closed loops, emerging from the north pole outside the magnet and entering the south pole, then passing through the magnet from south to north
They are straight parallel lines that never close on themselves
They start from the south pole and end at the north pole, never passing through the magnet
questions.e: Magnetic field lines are continuous closed loops. Outside the magnet they go from north pole to south pole, and inside the magnet they continue from south pole back to north pole, forming a complete loop. They never start or stop at a point.
questions.p: Magnetic field lines na closed loop wey no get start or end. Outside di magnet, dem dey comot from north go south, and inside di magnet dem dey continue from south go north to complete di loop.

questions.q: A straight metal rod of length 0.8 m moves with a velocity of 5 m/s at right angles to a uniform magnetic field of flux density 0.25 T. Calculate the electromotive force (EMF) induced in the rod.
questions.e: For motional EMF, e = B x L x v. Substituting values: e = 0.25 x 0.8 x 5 = 1.0 V. This is the standard formula for a rod moving perpendicular to a magnetic field.
questions.p: For motional EMF, we use e = B x L x v. If we put di numbers: e = 0.25 x 0.8 x 5 = 1.0 V. Na straightforward formula wen rod dey move perpendicular to di field.

questions.q: A coil of 200 turns is linked with a magnetic flux that changes uniformly from 2.0 x 10⁻³ Wb to 8.0 x 10⁻³ Wb in 0.3 seconds. Calculate the average EMF induced in the coil.
questions.e: By Faraday's law, EMF = N x (change in flux)/(time). Change in flux = 8.0x10⁻³ - 2.0x10⁻³ = 6.0x10⁻³ Wb. EMF = 200 x (6.0x10⁻³)/0.3 = 200 x 0.02 = 4.0 V.
questions.p: Faraday law talk say EMF = N x (change in flux)/(time). Di change in flux na 8.0x10⁻³ - 2.0x10⁻³ = 6.0x10⁻³ Wb. So EMF = 200 x (6.0x10⁻³)/0.3 = 4.0 V.

questions.q: A straight current-carrying conductor of length 0.6 m carries a current of 3.0 A and is placed in a uniform magnetic field of flux density 0.5 T such that the conductor makes an angle of 30° with the field. Calculate the magnitude of the force on the conductor.
questions.e: The force on a current-carrying conductor is F = B x I x L x sin(theta), where theta is the angle between the conductor and the field. F = 0.5 x 3.0 x 0.6 x sin(30°) = 0.5 x 3.0 x 0.6 x 0.5 = 0.45 N. Candidates who forget the sine factor or use the wrong angle get the wrong answer.
questions.p: Di force for current-carrying wire na F = B x I x L x sin(theta), wia theta na di angle between di wire and di field. F = 0.5 x 3.0 x 0.6 x sin(30°) = 0.5 x 3.0 x 0.6 x 0.5 = 0.45 N. If you forget di sin factor or use wrong angle, you go miss am.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly defines simple harmonic motion?
o: Motion in which the displacement is directly proportional to the time elapsed
Motion in which the velocity is constant and directed towards a fixed point
Motion in which the acceleration is constant and directed away from a fixed point
Motion in which the acceleration is proportional to the displacement from a fixed point and is always directed towards that point
questions.e: Simple harmonic motion is defined by a restoring force (and hence acceleration) that is proportional to displacement from a fixed equilibrium point and always points back towards that point. This is the defining feature that distinguishes SHM from other types of motion.
questions.p: Simple harmonic motion na when the force wey dey pull the body back (so acceleration) dey match the distance e don move from the center point, and e dey always push am back to that center. Na this one make SHM different from other motion.

questions.q: A simple pendulum completes one full oscillation in 2.0 seconds. Taking g = 10 m/s² and pi² as approximately 10, calculate the length of the pendulum.
questions.e: Using T = 2pi × √(L/g), we rearrange to get L = g × T²/(4pi²). Substituting g = 10, T = 2.0 and pi² = 10 gives L = (10 x 4)/(4 x 10) = 1.0 m.
questions.p: We use T = 2pi × √(L/g) and change am to L = g × T²/(4pi²). If we put g=10, T=2.0 and pi²=10, we go get L = (10 x 4)/(4 x 10) = 1.0 m.

questions.q: A particle performs simple harmonic motion with amplitude 10 cm and period 4.0 s. Using π = 3.14, calculate the speed of the particle when its displacement from the equilibrium position is 6 cm.
questions.e: Angular frequency w = 2pi/T = 2pi/4 = π/2 rad/s. Speed is given by v = w × √(A² - x²) = (π/2) × √(10² - 6²) = (π/2) × 8 = 4pi, which equals about 12.56 cm/s.
questions.p: Angular frequency w = 2pi/T = π/2 rad/s. We dey find speed with v = w × √(A² - x²) = (π/2) × √(100-36) = (π/2) × 8 = 4pi, wey be like 12.56 cm/s.

questions.q: A simple pendulum has a period of 3.2 s on Earth where g = 10 m/s². The same pendulum is taken to the Moon where the acceleration due to gravity is 1.6 m/s². Calculate its new period on the Moon, correct to one decimal place.
questions.e: Since T is proportional to 1/√g for a fixed length, T_moon = T_earth × √(g_earth/g_moon) = 3.2√(10/1.6) = 3.2√6.25 = 3.2 × 2.5 = 8.0 s. The weaker gravity on the Moon makes the pendulum swing more slowly, so the period increases.

questions.q: Which of the following radioactive emissions has the greatest ionizing power but the least penetrating power, being stopped by a thin sheet of paper or a few centimetres of air?

questions.q: A radioactive isotope used in a Lagos teaching hospital has an initial mass of 800 g. If its half-life is 6 hours, what mass of the isotope remains after 18 hours, assuming no other process removes the material?
questions.e: 18 hours divided by the half-life of 6 hours gives 3 half-lives. After each half-life the mass halves, so 800 g becomes 400 g, then 200 g, then 100 g after 3 half-lives.

questions.q: The half-life of a certain radioactive substance is 20 days. Using ln 2 = 0.693, calculate its decay constant correct to 3 decimal places.

questions.q: An archaeologist found a wooden carving from an old settlement near Ile-Ife whose carbon-14 activity is only 12.5% of the activity measured in a freshly cut piece of the same type of wood. If the half-life of carbon-14 is 5730 years, estimate the age of the carving.

questions.q: In Einstein's photoelectric equation, hf = W0 + KE(max), what does the term W0 represent?

The frequency of the incident radiation
The total energy carried by the incident photon
The minimum energy needed to free an electron from the metal surface (the work function)
questions.e: W0 is called the work function. It is the least amount of energy an electron needs to escape from the metal surface. The photon energy hf supplies this, and any extra energy becomes the electron's kinetic energy.

questions.q: A photon of energy 4.5 eV strikes a metal surface whose work function is 1.9 eV. Using mass of electron m = 9.11 x 10⁻³¹ kg and 1 eV = 1.6 x 10⁻¹⁹ J, calculate the maximum speed of the emitted photoelectron.
questions.e: Max KE = 4.5 eV - 1.9 eV = 2.6 eV = 2.6 x 1.6x10⁻¹⁹ = 4.16x10⁻¹⁹ J. Using KE = 1/2 m v², v = √(2KE/m) = √(2 x 4.16x10⁻¹⁹ / 9.11x10⁻³¹) which gives about 9.6 x 10⁵ m/s.
questions.p: Max KE = 4.5 eV - 1.9 eV = 2.6 eV = 2.6 x 1.6x10⁻¹⁹ = 4.16x10⁻¹⁹ J. From KE = 1/2 m v², v = √(2KE/m) = √(2 x 4.16x10⁻¹⁹ / 9.11x10⁻³¹) wey give about 9.6 x 10⁵ m/s.
